On FineCops-Ref, A4 lags S4 by 0.52 percentage points in IoU@0.5 (95% CI [0.12, 0.95]), while A8 recovers this gap and leads S4 by 0.26 points. FineCops levels do not show a monotonic gap trend. A4 reduces trainable decoder parameters by 44.4% and cached-decoder latency by 10.1%, though end-to-end latency remains dominated by the backbone. Note: conclusions apply to the trainable grounding decoder, not a complete attention-only VLM.

Conclusion: In frozen-VLM visual grounding, FFN in the decoder is not consistently essential; carefully designed attention-only decoders can achieve comparable performance with meaningful efficiency gains. The FFN contribution is dataset-dependent, with occasional small gains that may be recovered by adding more attention blocks (A8).

Abstract: Do feed-forward networks (FFNs) in visual grounding decoders add essential computation once a pretrained vision-language model has already encoded image and language context? We compare a four-block attention-only decoder (A4), a matched four-block attention-plus-FFN decoder (S4), and an eight-block attention-only parameter control (A8) over frozen VLM features. A4 matches or slightly exceeds S4 on RefCOCOg and Ref-Adv-s. FineCops-Ref reveals a small A4 deficit of 0.52 percentage points at IoU@0.5 (95% CI [0.12, 0.95] in favor of S4), but A8 recovers it and finishes 0.26 points above S4. Official FineCops levels do not show a monotonic increase in the gap. A4 reduces trainable decoder parameters by 44.4% and cached-decoder latency by 10.1%, although end-to-end latency remains backbone-dominated. These results concern the trainable grounding decoder, not a complete attention-only VLM.

</details>


### [50] [SA-GEM: Scale-Adaptive and Geospatial Evidence-Modulated Token Pruning for Efficient Remote Sensing Large Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15075)
*Kexin Ma,Jing Xiao,Bowen Xing,Liang Liao,Chia-Wen Lin*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SA-GEM: Scale-Adaptive and Geospatial Evidence-Modulated Token Pruning for RS-LVLMs; introduces a query-driven resolution router and a geospatial evidence modulator to jointly optimize token granularity and preservation, yielding accuracy and efficiency gains over existing pruning methods; on XLRS-Bench, outperforms GeoLLaVA-8K by 2.3% accuracy and 2.4x speedup.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Earth observation RS-LVLMs suffer from quadratic growth of visual tokens with high-resolution inputs; current pruning relies on scale-agnostic policies and isolated cues, compromising task-aligned granularity and holistic evidence preservation.

Method: Propose SA-GEM, a plug-and-play framework: a lightweight router selects input resolution based on query-dependent token granularity; a token importance modulator jointly models task relevance, spatial structure, and local redundancy to preserve holistic geospatial evidence.

Result: SA-GEM achieves consistent gains in accuracy and efficiency over existing pruning methods across benchmarks; on XLRS-Bench it surpasses GeoLLaVA-8K by 2.3% in accuracy with 2.4× total inference speedup.

Conclusion: Higher resolution is not universally beneficial; after achieving sufficient granularity, token quality matters more than token quantity; SA-GEM provides a principled, scalable approach to RS-LVLM token pruning with strong empirical gains.

Abstract: RS-LVLMs have advanced multimodal understanding of Earth observation imagery, yet their performance is fundamentally constrained by high-resolution processing, as visual token counts grow quadratically with linear input resolution while important visual evidence is inherently sparse and increasingly diluted across the expanded sequence. Existing token pruning methods largely rely on scale-agnostic resolution policies and isolated importance cues, limiting task-aligned granularity adaptation and holistic evidence preservation. To address this, we present Scale-Adaptive and Geospatial Evidence-Modulated Token Pruning (SA-GEM), a plug-and-play framework that unifies task-adaptive token granularity allocation with holistic geospatial token importance modulation. Specifically, a lightweight router selects the resolution based on query-dependent token granularity, while a token importance modulator jointly models task relevance, spatial structure, and local redundancy to preserve holistic geospatial evidence. We show that higher resolution is not universally beneficial and, once sufficient granularity is reached, token quality matters more than token quantity. Experiments across various benchmarks demonstrate that SA-GEM achieves consistent gains in both accuracy and efficiency over existing pruning methods. On XLRS-Bench, it surpasses GeoLLaVA-8K by 2.3% in accuracy with a 2.4 times total inference speedup.

</details>


### [51] [Distribution-free false-alarm calibration and chance-corrected spatial evaluation for industrial anomaly detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15090)
*Jie Deng*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes a distribution-free upper tolerance threshold plus a paired-minus-crossed spatial test to quantify spatial-evidence lift over empirical chance for defect localization, showing limited but meaningful lift for some detectors and promoting reporting of spatial evidence alongside AUROC and mask overlap.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AUROC and raw overlap do not constrain false-alarm rates at a chosen threshold; overlap can be inflated by recurrent defect locations and mask geometry. A distribution-free, threshold-aware measure of spatial evidence is needed to assess detector performance more reliably.

Method: Introduce a distribution-free upper tolerance threshold and a paired-minus-crossed spatial test. The test compares each detector's score-contributing locations against the matched defect mask and against masks from other images, yielding a spatial-evidence lift relative to empirical chance overlap. Evaluate three detectors on 120 point-defect images from three ISP-AD modalities across three fixed splits; report bootstrap CIs for lifts. Extend analysis to an independent Magnetic Tile Defect dataset (two memory-based detectors: WRN50 patch memory and ViT-B/16 patch memory) with permutation tests. Also perform exact sample planning to determine the number of calibration normals needed for distribution-free confidence at various target false-positive rates; examine the effect of restricting crosses to the same defect class.

Result: On 378 alarms, 230 overlapped the matched mask; most paired and crossed rates are similar across detector-modality cells; only DINOv2-ASM shows a positive 95% bootstrap lower bound for lift (0.259, 95% CI 0.159–0.347). On Magnetic Tile Defect data, lifts are 0.203 (0.169–0.236) for WRN50 patch memory and 0.231 (0.202–0.262) for ViT-B/16 patch memory, with one-sided permutation p = 1e-5 for both; restricting crosses to the same defect class yields lifts of 0.185 and 0.210. Exact sample planning indicates that with 150 calibration normals, a 95% distribution-free claim requires target FPR ≥1.98%; a 1% target needs at least 299 normals.

Conclusion: The results justify reporting operating-point performance and chance-corrected spatial evidence alongside AUROC and raw mask overlap, as it provides a more robust assessment of spatial localization performance and guards against inflated overlap claims.

Abstract: Studies of industrial visual inspection commonly report the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the overlap between anomaly maps and defect masks. Neither measure specifies the false-alarm rate at a selected threshold, while recurrent defect locations and mask geometry can inflate overlap. We combine a distribution-free upper tolerance threshold with a paired-minus-crossed spatial test. This test compares each detector's score-contributing locations with the matched defect mask and with masks from other images; the difference in rates defines spatial-evidence lift relative to the empirical chance-overlap rate. We evaluate three detectors on 120 point-defect images from three ISP-AD modalities and three fixed data splits. Of 378 alarms, 230 overlap the matched mask. Paired and crossed rates are nevertheless similar in eight of nine detector--modality cells; only DINOv2--ASM has a positive 95\% bootstrap lower bound (lift 0.259, 95\% interval 0.159--0.347). On the independent Magnetic Tile Defect dataset, the same analysis gives lifts of 0.203 (0.169--0.236) for Wide ResNet-50 (WRN50) patch memory and 0.231 (0.202--0.262) for Vision Transformer B/16 (ViT-B/16) patch memory, with one-sided permutation $p=10^{-5}$ for both. When crossed masks are restricted to the same defect class, the lifts remain 0.185 and 0.210. Exact sample planning shows that, with 150 calibration normals, a 95\%-confidence distribution-free claim is supported only for target false-positive rates of 1.98\% or higher; a 1\% target requires at least 299 normals. The results support reporting operating-point performance and chance-corrected spatial evidence alongside AUROC and raw mask overlap.

</details>


### [52] [MODAL: Multi-Modal Object Re-ID via Model-Driven Sparse Decoupling and Text-Image Differential Filtering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15096)
*Chengbo Huang,Jun-Jie Huang,Long Lan,Tianrui Liu,Xueqiong Li,Yuanxi Peng,Xinwang Liu,Meng Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MODAL introduces a model-driven, unrolled multi-modal sparse coding framework for robust multi-modal object re-ID, achieving explicit uni-/bi-/tri-modal disentanglement, modality-aware subspace activation for incomplete modalities, and text-guided filtering, yielding state-of-the-art results on four datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address entangled multi-modal representations and distribution shifts when modalities are missing, hindering cross-camera Re-ID performance.

Method: Develops a Multi-modal Feature Sparse Decoupling module via coupled sparse coding with an unrolled network; decomposes features into uni-modal-specific, bi-modal shared, and tri-modal shared components; employs Modality-Aware Subspace Activation to tolerate missing modalities; introduces Text-Image Differential Filtering to suppress task-irrelevant responses using coarse textual semantics.

Result: Empirical evaluation on four datasets shows state-of-the-art accuracy and improved transparency of representations, with robustness to incomplete-modality scenarios.

Conclusion: Principled feature disentanglement and targeted cross-modal integration yield improved Re-ID performance and interpretability; framework could extend to additional modalities and real-world deployment; future work may explore more efficient optimization and broader modality combinations.

Abstract: Multi-modal object re-identification (Re-ID) aims to facilitate cross-camera object retrieval in complex environments by leveraging complementary information from visual (e.g., RGB, NIR, TIR) and textual modalities. However, existing approaches often lack principled feature disentanglement and coherent multi-modal integration, leading to entangled representations that introduce cross-modal conflicts, obscure discriminative cues, and suffer distribution shift under modality-missing conditions. To tackle these challenges, we propose MODAL, a novel multi-modal object re-identification framework, grounded in coupled sparse coding theory and differential suppression principles. A core component of MODAL is a Multi-modal Feature Sparse Decoupling module, developed in a model-driven deep unrolling manner based on multi-modal coupled sparse coding. It explicitly decomposes multi-modal features into uni-modal specific, bi-modal and tri-modal shared representations, thereby achieving more transparent and effective feature disentanglement. Benefiting from the principled feature disentanglement, MODAL naturally mitigates performance degradation in incomplete-modality scenarios via a Modality-Aware Subspace Activation that selectively activates only the consistently shared subspaces. Moreover, we propose a Text-Image Differential Filtering module that leverages coarse-grained textual semantics to adaptively suppress task-irrelevant responses in the decoupled visual representations, thereby enhancing discriminative information. Extensive experiments on four datasets demonstrate that MODAL achieves state-of-the-art performance with superior transparency.

</details>


### [53] [ProjFormer: Point Cloud Completion via Geometric-Projective Transformer and Cross-Modal Semantic Constraints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15104)
*Sheng Liu,Meng Wang,Ruihui Li,Huilong Pi,Zhuo Tang,Kenli Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ProjFormer introduces a cross-modal 2D-3D framework for point cloud completion that uses a deterministic projection-based view attention and a geometry-aware routing network for adaptive fusion, achieving competitive results with a lightweight design.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Multi-view 2D semantics help but current fusion is often learned-attention-based and fixed, leading to geometric inconsistency and limited adaptability in ill-posed, sparse point cloud completion.

Method: A Projective Guided View Attention module aligns 3D points with multi-view features via deterministic projection for geometry-consistent aggregation. A geometry-aware routing network then performs point-wise adaptive fusion of structural and observation-driven features for progressive refinement.

Result: Experiments demonstrate competitive completion performance with improved structural completeness under a lightweight architecture.

Conclusion: Explicit geometry-consistent 2D-3D interaction through projection and adaptive routing can enhance efficiency and structure in point cloud completion, offering a viable lightweight alternative to heavier fusion approaches.

Abstract: Point cloud completion is inherently ill-posed due to severe sparsity and ambiguity in partial observations. Existing multi-view methods alleviate this by incorporating 2D semantics, but often rely on learned attention and fixed fusion, which lack geometric consistency and adaptability. We propose ProjFormer, a cross-modal framework that enforces geometry-consistent 2D-3D interaction through explicit projection and adaptive feature routing. A Projective Guided View Attention module aligns 3D points with multi-view features via deterministic projection, enabling efficient and geometrically consistent aggregation. Building on this, a geometry-aware routing network performs point-wise adaptive fusion of structural and observation-driven features for progressive refinement. Experiments show that, under a lightweight design, ProjFormer delivers competitive performance with improved structural completeness.

</details>


### [54] [CETalk: Continuous Valence-Arousal Control for Audio-Driven 3D Talking Head Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15110)
*Peng Jia,Li Dai,Zhen Xiao,Xueliang Liu,Jia Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A continuous-Valence–Arousal conditioned framework CETalk for audio-driven 3D facial animation that achieves superior lip-sync and emotional expressiveness via dynamic emotion modulation, multi-scale temporal modeling, and adaptive fusion, evaluated on a large 3D-VA-MEAD dataset.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Limitations of discrete-emotion models and misalignment between audio articulation and emotional dynamics; need for continuous affect representation and better temporal alignment.

Method: CETalk with (1) Dynamic Emotion Modulation Module; (2) Multi-Scale Temporal Modeling with parallel branches; (3) Dynamic Fusion Mechanism with adaptive gating; data: 3D-VA-MEAD with automatically estimated VA annotations and reconstructed motions.

Result: Outperforms SOTA in lip-sync accuracy and emotional expressiveness; enables smooth, controllable emotion transitions.

Conclusion: Demonstrates effectiveness of continuous VA conditioning for audio-driven 3D facial animation and provides a scalable dataset for VA-based evaluation.

Abstract: Emotional 3D talking head generation aims to synthesize expressive facial animations with accurate lip synchronization. However, existing methods often rely on discrete emotion categories, which fail to capture the continuous evolution of affect. They also overlook the temporal frequency mismatch between audio articulation and emotional expression. In this paper, we propose CETalk, an audio-driven 3D facial animation framework conditioned on continuous Valence--Arousal (VA) representations for fine-grained emotion control. CETalk predicts a sequence of FLAME parameters through three key components: a Dynamic Emotion Modulation Module that adaptively scales emotional intensity using audio-derived cues; a Multi-Scale Temporal Modeling mechanism that employs parallel branches to decouple high-frequency articulatory movements from low-frequency emotional dynamics; and a Dynamic Fusion Mechanism that integrates these multi-scale features via an adaptive gating network. To support training and evaluation, we construct 3D-VA-MEAD, a large-scale dataset with automatically estimated VA annotations and reconstructed 3D facial motions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CETalk outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both lip-sync accuracy and emotional expressiveness, while enabling smooth and controllable emotion transitions.

</details>


### [55] [Fast Test-Time Refinement for Robust Learned Image Compression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15113)
*Jiaming Liang,Chi-Man Pun,Weisi Lin*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A systematic study of learned image compression (LIC) reveals an Asymmetric Adversarial Trajectory (AAT) and proposes Fast Test-Time Refinement (FTTR) with a 2D Tube Model to improve robustness against adaptive attacks; robustness arises from contraction of adversarial regions via Input-as-Label, with code released.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: LIC offers strong rate-distortion (RD) performance but suffers from high adversarial vulnerability; test-time refinement (TTR) is costly and not well understood; there is a lack of white-box evaluation and evaluation against diverse attack objectives; a principled, efficient defense is needed.

Method: 1) Characterize adversarial dynamics as Asymmetric Adversarial Trajectory (AAT). 2) Propose a two-dimensional Tube Model to explain AAT. 3) Develop Fast Test-Time Refinement (FTTR) that refines at test time with limited iterations. 4) Argue robustness stems from Input-as-Label contraction rather than obfuscated gradients. 5) Evaluate against strong adaptive attacks across multiple LIC systems. 6) Release code.

Result: FTTR demonstrates practical robustness improvements under adaptive attacks across several LIC models. The defense behavior is explained by the Tube Model and the Input-as-Label induced contraction of adversarial regions, not gradient obfuscation. The work provides theoretical insight and empirical validation, with code availability.

Conclusion: FTTR offers a practical, robust defense for LIC and advances understanding of adversarial dynamics in learned compression through AAT and the Tube Model, suggesting efficient defenses for standard-compliant codecs.

Abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) has demonstrated remarkable rate-distortion (RD) performance in benign settings. However, the high representational capacity endowed by deep neural networks (DNNs) comes at the expense of increased adversarial vulnerability. This hinders their adoption as trusted standardized codecs. Recent work has sketched test-time refinement (TTR) as a defense in gray-box scenarios, despite its original purpose of improving benign RD performance. Unfortunately, extensive iterations of TTR incur prohibitive overhead, while the robustness mechanism lacks theoretical understanding. Moreover, TTR has not been evaluated in white-box settings or against attacks beyond $\ell_2$-bounded rate and untargeted distortion objectives. To bridge these gaps, we present a systematic study. Our study reveals an Asymmetric Adversarial Trajectory (AAT) property in LIC systems: transitioning from adversarial to benign regions is significantly easier than the reverse process, where adversarial examples can often be roughly recovered within only 1-2 steps. We provide a two-dimensional Tube Model to explain this phenomenon. Based on AAT, we propose a Fast Test-Time Refinement (FTTR) framework for practical and robust LIC systems. We establish that the robustness arises from the contraction of adversarial regions induced by the Input-as-Label property of LIC systems, rather than from obfuscated gradients. Extensive evaluations with diverse strong adaptive attacks across multiple LIC systems demonstrate the promise of the proposed FTTR framework. The code is available at https://github.com/chinaliangjiaming/FTTR.git.

</details>


### [56] [Perspective-Invariant Attack with Enhanced Transferability of Adversarial Examples](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15115)
*Kaisheng Liang,Yiming Cao,Bin Xiao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A perspective-transformation-based input augmentation (PIA) with multi-DOF vertex sampling to enhance cross-model adversarial transferability; extended as PIA-Mix.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Adversarial examples transfer across models pose security risks; existing input transformations rely on local operations with limited degrees of freedom, neglecting global perspective changes from viewpoint variations; global perspective transformations could improve transferability and robustness against defenses and multimodal models.

Method: PIA introduces a multi-DOF vertex sampling strategy that spans the perspective transformation hierarchy from 2-DOF translation to 8-DOF projective mapping, generating geometrically diverse input variations to reduce perturbation overfitting to the surrogate and improve transferability. PIA-Mix extends PIA by maintaining a complementary transformation pool and efficiently combining perspective transformation with auxiliary transferability methods.

Result: Extensive experiments across diverse DNN architectures, defenses, and multimodal large language models show that PIA and PIA-Mix achieve superior transferability compared with state-of-the-art transfer-based attacks.

Conclusion: Utilizing global perspective transformations via multi-DOF vertex sampling significantly boosts adversarial transferability; PIA provides a robust, general framework, with PIA-Mix offering practical gains by integrating complementary transformations.

Abstract: Adversarial examples generated on a surrogate deep neural network (DNN) can often successfully fool other black-box DNN models. This cross-model transferability poses serious security threats to DNNs in practical applications. Input transformation techniques are widely used to enhance adversarial transferability by increasing the diversity of input images. However, existing methods primarily rely on local operations with limited degrees of freedom (DOF), such as block-wise shuffling and resizing, overlooking global perspective transformations that naturally arise from viewpoint changes. In this work, we propose a Perspective-Invariant Attack (PIA), which introduces a multi-DOF vertex sampling strategy that systematically covers the perspective transformation hierarchy from 2-DOF translation to 8-DOF projective mapping. By generating geometrically diverse input variations, PIA effectively reduces overfitting of adversarial perturbations to the surrogate model, thereby improving adversarial transferability. We further propose PIA-Mix, a generic extension that maintains a complementary transformation pool and efficiently combines our perspective transformation with auxiliary methods for improved transferability. Extensive experiments involving various DNN architectures, advanced defense mechanisms, and multimodal large language models (LLMs) demonstrate that PIA and PIA-Mix outperform state-of-the-art transfer-based attacks.

</details>


### [57] [HOIMask: Towards Generative Masked Modeling for Human Object Interaction Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15141)
*Yihong Ji,Jinsong Zhang,He Hu,Hongbo Xu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: HOIMask introduces a discrete-space, token-based HOI motion model that uses HOI Vector Quantization and masked generative modeling with a transformer, plus contact-aware inference guidance, to outperform diffusion-based HOI generation in realism and semantic alignment.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Diffusion-based HOI generation suffers from artifacts and unstable interaction quality due to error accumulation during iterative denoising; a discrete, token-based approach with explicit contact signals can improve spatio-temporal coherence.

Method: Encode motion sequences and contact signals into discrete 2D token maps via HOI Vector Quantization; employ a generative masked transformer to model spatial-temporal and interaction dependencies; apply contact-aware reconstruction guidance in discrete space during inference to fuse contact signals and refine HOI tokens for coherence.

Result: HOIMask outperforms state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods, producing more realistic and semantically aligned HOI motions.

Conclusion: A novel discrete-space, masked generative framework for HOI motion modeling that leverages HOI VQ and contact-aware guidance to achieve higher coherence and plausibility than diffusion-based approaches.

Abstract: Diffusion-based methods have dominated the HOI generation, as they enable critical contact fusions or signals to guide the diffusion process. However, they often result in high artifacts and unstable interaction quality due to error accumulation during iterative denoising. In this work, we propose HOIMask, the first generative masked framework for modeling HOI motion in discrete space. HOIMask first encodes both motion sequences and contact-aware signals into discrete 2D human and object token maps via HOI Vector Quantization (VQ), preserving fine-grained spatial-temporal structure beyond conventional 1D representations. On this basis, a generative masked modeling framework is employed to jointly capture human-object interaction dynamics, leveraging a transformer architecture designed to model complex spatial-temporal and interaction dependencies. To generate more coherent and physically plausible motions, we further introduce a novel contact-aware reconstruction guidance in discrete space during inference, which fuses contact signals to optimize HOI tokens that forces the generated motion with higher spatio-temporal consistency. With craftily designed motion interaction tokens, dedicated architecture and guidance strategy, HOIMask outperforms state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods, generating more realistic and semantically aligned HOI motions. Please refer to https://jyhflash.github.io/HOIMask/ for more results.

</details>


### [58] [A Unified Backbone--Expert Framework with Relation-Token and Residual--Classifier Interfaces for Automatic Modulation Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15160)
*Zhixiang Deng,Houbiao Li,Zongyong Cui*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Unified backbone-expert AMR framework with a common convolutional state-space backbone and two specialized interfaces; short sequences use lag-aware complex-plane relation tokens; long sequences use gated multi-scale refinement and fixed-averaging classifier; strong results on RML2016.10b (67.28±0.14%) and HisarMod2019 (87.19±0.77%). Ablations across seeds and configurations support expert-interface decoupling.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AMR performance is hampered by representation bottlenecks when observation lengths vary; a single architecture often fails to maximize accuracy across short and long sequences. A decoupled, expert-interface design could tailor processing to sequence length.

Method: Propose a unified backbone-expert framework: a common convolutional state-space backbone; for short sequences, inject lag-aware complex-plane descriptors as relation tokens before encoding; for long sequences, apply a gated multi-scale residual refinement module to adjust feature maps, coupled with a fixed-averaging classifier to leverage complementary evidence. Evaluate via three-seed ablations, native-length cross-configuration tests, and controlled window studies to demonstrate robustness of expert-interface decoupling.

Result: Reported accuracies: 67.28 ± 0.14% (RML2016.10b); 87.19 ± 0.77% (HisarMod2019) across three runs. Ablation and cross-configuration tests corroborate the benefit of decoupling the backbone from the interfaces across sequence lengths.

Conclusion: Expert-interface decoupling with a unified backbone yields robust AMR performance across short and long observation lengths, validating the proposed design and its robustness across seeds and configurations.

Abstract: Automatic modulation recognition (AMR) faces distinct representation bottlenecks under varying observation lengths, where a single model architecture often fails to excel. To address this, we propose a unified backbone-expert framework with a common convolutional state-space backbone and two specialized interfaces. For short sequences, we inject explicit lag-aware complex-plane descriptors as relation tokens before encoding to compensate for information loss. For long sequences, we design a gated multi-scale residual refinement module to correct the feature map, combined with a fixed-averaging classifier collaboration to harness complementary evidence. Our framework achieves overall average accuracies of 67.28 \pm 0.14% on RML2016.10b and 87.19 \pm 0.77% on HisarMod2019 (mean \pm sample standard deviation over three runs), respectively. The framework's efficacy is further validated through three-seed ablations, native-length cross-configuration tests, and controlled window studies, confirming the benefit of expert-interface decoupling over one-size-fits-all architectures.

</details>


### [59] [From "What-If" to "What-Is": Counterfactual Thinking-Inspired Semantic Alignment for Visual Brain Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15163)
*Kaitao Yan,Chi Liu,Congcong Zhu,Huajie Chen,Gengshen Wu,Minghao Wang,Xiaotong Han,Tianqing Zhu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ConceptAlign aligns decoded visual tokens with a frozen text-embedding space to enforce semantic alignment with ground-truth captions and to separate plausible but incorrect interpretations via counterfactuals, using a margin-based objective. It improves reconstruction quality, counterfactual semantic discrimination, and representational alignment on the Natural Scenes Dataset compared to MindEye2, with thorough ablations and human validation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address semantic errors in visual brain decoding caused by strong generative priors that can hallucinate objects/attributes/relations when decoded representations are underspecified. Traditional image-centric metrics miss semantic mistakes.

Method: Pool decoded visual tokens into a frozen text-embedding space; align with ground-truth caption; generate offline counterfactual alternatives via an LLM that modify one critical object/attribute/relation while keeping the scene; train with a margin-based objective that enforces fine-grained semantic boundaries between observed stimulus and plausible but incorrect interpretations; avoid LLM calls during inference; evaluate with a three-level semantic framework; dataset: Natural Scenes Dataset; backbone: MindEye2; include ablations with negative sources and human/LLM alternatives.

Result: Improves reconstruction metrics, counterfactual semantic discrimination, and representational alignment versus the MindEye2 backbone; ablations and human evaluations support robustness; favorable results in limited-data and cross-subject settings.

Conclusion: ConceptAlign offers a semantically grounded, counterfactual-aware framework for visual brain decoding that enhances both reconstruction fidelity and semantic interpretability, with a rigorous three-tier evaluation and robust empirical support.

Abstract: Visual brain decoding reconstructs visual content perceived by a person from neural measurements such as fMRI, providing a computational approach to studying how visual information is represented in the brain. Recent multimodal representations and diffusion priors have improved reconstruction realism. However, visually plausible reconstructions may contain incorrect objects, attributes, or relations because a strong generative prior can complete content not sufficiently specified by the decoded representation. Conventional reconstruction metrics mainly assess the final image and may therefore obscure such semantic errors. We propose ConceptAlign, a counterfactual semantic alignment framework for visual brain decoding. ConceptAlign pools decoded visual tokens and projects them into a frozen text-embedding space, aligning the representation with the ground-truth caption while separating it from scene-preserving near-miss alternatives. Generated offline by an LLM, these alternatives modify one critical object, attribute, or relation while retaining the scene. A margin-based objective learns fine-grained semantic boundaries between the observed stimulus and plausible but incorrect interpretations without requiring LLM calls during inference. We introduce a systematic three-level semantic evaluation framework covering foundational discriminability, counterfactual description discrimination, and representational geometry. Experiments on the Natural Scenes Dataset show that ConceptAlign improves reconstruction measures, counterfactual semantic discrimination, and representational alignment over the MindEye2 backbone. Matched negative-source ablations, independent LLM and human-written alternatives, and human evaluation support the effectiveness and robustness of the supervision, with favorable patterns in fine-grained conflicts, limited-data decoding, and cross-subject structure.

</details>


### [60] [Beyond Natural-Image Foundation Models: Benchmarking Satellite Pretraining for Ophthalmic Image Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15195)
*Lovre Antonio Budimir,Mingya Alexa Gong,Alyssa Foong Quinney,Ivana Matovinović,Yukun Zhou,Pearse A. Keane,Sven Lončarić,Marinko V. Šarunić*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Satellite-pretrained DINOv3 models yield strong ophthalmic performance, rivaling or surpassing medical baselines, without using medical data.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To mitigate data scarcity, privacy issues, and high costs in medical imaging; address distribution shift when shipping medical models pretrained on general natural images; explore privacy-friendly, domain-aligned pretraining with satellite imagery.

Method: Compare DINOv3-SAT493m (satellite-pretrained on 493M images) against DINOv3-LVD1689m (natural-image-pretrained on 1.7B images) and two medical baselines (DINOv3-RETFound, MAE-RETFound) across multiple ophthalmic imaging modalities, focusing on high-resolution en face vascular-rich inputs.

Result: Satellite pretraining outperforms natural-image pretraining for ophthalmic tasks; on several tasks, matches or exceeds medical specialists, despite using no medical data, particularly for high-resolution en face inputs.

Conclusion: Satellite imagery is a viable pretraining domain for MedVFMs, enabling strong performance without medical data and potentially reducing privacy and data-collection constraints; supports benchmarking satellite-based pretraining for ophthalmology.

Abstract: Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) have emerged as a promising approach in medical imaging, producing broadly applicable systems that can be efficiently adapted across diverse imaging modalities, anatomical regions, and clinical tasks. However, VFMs require extensive training data, and their progress in medical image analysis is constrained by limited data availability, privacy concerns, and high development costs. To alleviate these constraints, medical VFMs (MedVFMs) are often built upon weights from generalist models pretrained on vast amounts of publicly available natural images, introducing a substantial distribution shift for medical task adaptation. To address this, we propose satellite imagery as a novel pretraining domain for MedVFM development and benchmarking, motivated by its closer visual alignment with medical data and its freedom from the privacy constraints that limit medical datasets. Across multiple ophthalmic imaging modalities, we compare DINOv3-SAT493m pretrained on 493 million satellite images against DINOv3-LVD1689m pretrained on 1.7 billion natural images, together with two medical specialist baselines: DINOv3-RETFound and MAE-RETFound. Our experiments show that satellite imagery is a stronger pretraining source than natural images for ophthalmic tasks, particularly on en face vascular-rich modalities. On several tasks, satellite pretraining matches or exceeds the medical specialists on high-resolution en face inputs, despite using no medical data.

</details>


### [61] [Anchor-Regularized Adaptation for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection with DINOv3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15196)
*Hyeongjun Choi,Juhun Lee,Davide Cozzolino,Luisa Verdoliva,Simon S. Woo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ARA uses Low-Rank Adaptation with a frozen anchor classifier to exploit pixel-artifact cues while preserving the pre-trained representation, achieving SOTA across nine benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand why linear probes on frozen DINOv3 generalize with misaligned data and to overcome the limits of relying on misaligned data for artifact cues by enabling complementary supervision without distorting the pre-trained representation.

Method: Empirical analysis of misaligned vs aligned data effects on DINOv3; introduce Anchor-Regularized Adaptation (ARA) which uses LoRA to capture pixel-level artifacts while freezing an anchor classifier to maintain the original representation structure.

Result: ARA achieves state-of-the-art performance on nine diverse benchmarks, showing that combining misaligned and aligned data via the proposed regularization improves detection without sacrificing generalization.

Conclusion: ARA provides a practical framework to jointly leverage misaligned and aligned data by decoupling artifact-specific adaptation from the core representation, preserving generalization while enhancing sensitivity to pixel-artifact cues.

Abstract: Recent works in AI-generated image detection have shown that careful training data alignment can improve generalization by removing spurious correlations. However, linear probes on frozen DINOv3 representations achieve remarkably strong performance even when trained on misaligned datasets. Motivated by this result, we analyze the underlying rationale and the limits of this generalization. We find that frozen DINOv3 performs well because its decisions rely on features that faithfully represent the space of authentic images. At the same time, its final layer is less effective at capturing the subtle pixel-artifact cues that can be emphasized by aligned training data. We further observe that naively mixing aligned and misaligned data during adaptation improves sensitivity to such cues but at the cost of distorting the pre-trained representation, limiting generalization. To address this issue, we propose Anchor-Regularized Adaptation (ARA). We apply Low-Rank Adaptation to capture pixel-level artifacts while leveraging a frozen anchor classifier to avoid deviations from the original representation structure. This allows the model to exploit pixel-artifact cues without sacrificing generalization. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on nine diverse and challenging benchmarks, indicating that ARA enables complementary supervision from misaligned and aligned data for more effective detection.

</details>


### [62] [TERRA: A Hierarchical Parallel Training and Memory Orchestration Framework for High-Resolution AI-based Earth Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15211)
*Ruohan Wu,Ziqi Zhu,Yang Zhao,Jiarui Tang,Yingzhe Cui,Junshi Chen,Zhao Jing,Jun Shi,Hong An*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TERRA is a memory-efficient, scalable training framework for high-resolution Earth forecasting that combines SAWSTP sampling-aware parallelism with MO rollout-aware memory orchestration to enable very large transformer models and long rollout finetuning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome memory bottlenecks and limited system support when training high-resolution, transformer-based Earth forecasting models that couple convolutional sampling with shifted-window attention, especially for long rollout finetuning.

Method: Introduce TERRA with Sampling-Aware Window, Sequence, and Tensor Parallelism (SAWSTP) to preserve spatial layouts for sampling modules and route tokens into topology-aware ragged window layouts. Add Memory Orchestration (MO) for rollout-aware checkpoint planning and activation offloading. Validate on 1/12° GLORYS Wenhai workload, scaling to 11.4B parameters on 96 H200 GPUs and achieving high FLOPS with strong/weak scaling; compare MO with checkpoint-only policies.

Result: Demonstrated memory-efficient, high-throughput training of very large high-resolution forecasting models. TERRA achieves up to 39.76 PFLOPS, 65.0% strong-scaling, 94.1% weak-scaling, and supports models up to 11.4B parameters on 96 GPUs. MO reduces peak memory by 32.2–51.8% with up to 20% step-time overhead, enabling longer rollouts and smaller patch sizes for better accuracy.

Conclusion: TERRA provides a practical, scalable solution for memory-constrained, high-resolution Earth forecasting model training, enabling larger models and longer rollout finetuning with acceptable overhead.

Abstract: Training high-resolution AI-based Earth forecasting models is memory-intensive. Window-based Swin Transformers reduce the quadratic cost of global attention, but existing distributed systems such as AERIS primarily target pixel-level models and do not jointly support convolutional sampling modules and shifted-window execution. Long-lead rollout finetuning further increases activation memory. To address these challenges, we present TERRA, a hierarchical parallel training framework for high-resolution Earth forecasting. TERRA introduces Sampling-Aware Window, Sequence, and Tensor Parallelism (SAWSTP), which preserves spatially contiguous layouts for sampling modules and routes tokens into topology-aware ragged window layouts for Transformer execution. For long-lead finetuning, Memory Orchestration (MO) provides rollout-aware checkpoint planning and combines input buffering with budget-constrained activation offloading. Experiments on the $1/12^\circ$ GLORYS-based Wenhai workload show that TERRA supports models with up to 11.4B parameters on 96 H200 GPUs and sustains up to $39.76$ PFLOPS, achieving $65.0\%$ strong-scaling and $94.1\%$ weak-scaling efficiency. Compared with checkpoint-only policies, MO further reduces peak allocated GPU memory by $32.2\%$--$51.8\%$ with at most $20.0\%$ step-time overhead, which makes finetuning with smaller patch sizes and longer rollouts feasible for improved forecasting accuracy.

</details>


### [63] [DCA-MoE: Spatially Adaptive Cross-Layer Fusion and Density-Routed Experts for Crowd Counting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15213)
*Hao Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DCA-MoE introduces spatially adaptive fusion (SALF) and density-routed MoE (DR-MoE) on top of a frozen DINOv3 backbone for crowd counting, achieving competitive NWPU-Crowd results; results are dataset-dependent and require broader multi-seed evaluation for causal attribution.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome the limitation of spatially invariant feature fusion in multi-level decoders for crowd counting under severe perspective, scale, and occlusion variations by enabling content-dependent fusion and routing.

Method: Propose Spatially Adaptive Layer Fusion (SALF) predicting position-wise fusion weights across four aligned backbone features; Density-Routed Multi-Receptive-Field Experts (DR-MoE) assigns each location a soft mixture of local, mid-range, and large-context residual experts. An EBC-style head reconstructs block density; training uses DMCount supervision and an auxiliary routing-balance term; backbone remains frozen (DINOv3). Evaluated with DINOv3 ViT-L/16 and ViT-B/16 backbones.

Result: On NWPU-Crowd validation: strongest config (DINOv3 ViT-L/16) 31.7 MAE, 72.2 RMSE; matched ViT-B/16 full model 32.2 MAE, 75.9 RMSE. Cross-dataset results are mixed; several baselines report minima from single seeds. Indicates feasibility of spatially adaptive fusion and routing, but broader multi-seed paired evaluation is needed for causal attribution.

Conclusion: Spatially adaptive fusion and routing are feasible for crowd counting with a frozen DINOv3 backbone; robust causal attribution requires more extensive multi-seed, cross-dataset evaluation.

Abstract: Crowd counting must recover reliable local density under severe variations in perspective, head scale, occlusion, and background clutter. Although modern counting objectives provide strong spatial supervision, many multi-level decoders still use spatially invariant feature fusion and apply one receptive-field pattern to every location. We propose DCA-MoE, a framework that makes both decisions content dependent while retaining a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Spatially Adaptive Layer Fusion (SALF) predicts position-wise weights over four aligned backbone features, and Density-Routed Multi-Receptive-Field Experts (DR-MoE) assigns each location a soft mixture of local, mid-range, and large-context residual experts. An EBC-style head reconstructs block density, while DMCount supervision and an auxiliary routing-balance term train the decoder without updating the backbone. On the NWPU-Crowd validation split, the strongest paired configuration, based on DINOv3 ViT-L/16, obtains 31.7 MAE and 72.2 RMSE; the matched ViT-B/16 full model obtains a paired 32.2/75.9. Cross-dataset results remain mixed, and several component baselines currently report independently selected minima from a single seed. The evidence therefore supports the feasibility of spatially adaptive fusion and routing, while broader paired and multi-seed evaluation remains necessary for causal attribution.

</details>


### [64] [Self-Supervised Topologically Invariant Manifold Learning for Railway Image Quality Assessment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15217)
*Tingqiong Cui,Yibu Yang,Yang Li,Jiahao Fu,Xiaoliu Luo,Xu Wang,Mengzhu Wang,Siyuan Liu,Guanghui Huang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Self-supervised BIQA using topologically invariant manifold learning with boundary constraints to derive a pseudo-ground-truth without labels; demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer and resilience on an industrial dataset.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Overcome reliance on synthetic distortions and subjective annotations in BIQA to improve real-world generalization.

Method: Create progressive background dilution via random crops to form a monotonic quality manifold; linearized spatial moment projection to remove cropping distortions; monotonicity divergence filter to prune background-sensitive evaluators; select elite pool from 11 metrics; robust M-estimator with PC stabilizer to fuse metrics into q_PGT.

Result: Elite pool achieves superior zero-shot transfer on CSIQ, LIVEC, LIVE-2; CQU dataset shows manifold cosine similarity >0.999 and 100% survival under extreme stresses.

Conclusion: The framework yields cross-paradigm decoupling and topological resilience, delivering a statistically efficient pseudo-ground truth approaching CRLB.

Abstract: Existing blind image quality assessment (BIQA) methods typically rely on synthetic distortions and subjective annotations, limiting generalization in real-world domains. To address this, we propose a fully self-supervised BIQA framework based on topologically invariant manifold learning under boundary constraints, which constructs a stable quality reference without manual labels. The framework generates progressive background dilution scales via repeated random cropping around each target; exploiting the monotonic degradation of target information density across these scales, it establishes a self-constrained quality manifold. A linearized spatial moment projection eliminates geometric distortions from random cropping; then a monotonicity divergence filter prunes background-sensitive evaluators, isolating an elite pool \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{elite}}\). A robust M-estimator with a principal component stabilizer fuses the metrics into an asymptotically efficient pseudo-ground truth \(q_{\text{PGT}}\), contracting variance toward the Cramér-Rao lower bound. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that the elite evaluator pool, distilled from 11 baseline metrics, secures superior zero-shot transferability across standard synthetic and wild benchmarks (CSIQ, LIVEC, LIVE-2). Concurrently, deployments on the CQU Railway Rolling Stock Surveillance Dataset (2,797 images) yield a manifold cosine similarity \(>0.999\) and a 100.0\% survival rate under industrial extreme stresses, robustly validating its cross-paradigm decoupling and topological resilience.

</details>


### [65] [PersonaDrive: Controllable Trajectory Prediction with Multi-Dimensional Driving Personas](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15230)
*Chan Lee,Kimin Yun,Yuseok Bae,Seong Tae Kim,Jung Uk Kim*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A dataset and framework for persona-conditioned trajectory generation: PCT and PersonaDrive enable language-informed, axis-aligned control over Temporal Urgency and Ride Comfort, improving trajectory prediction over baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current benchmarks lack multi-dimensional persona annotations and controllability; single-urgency labels fail to distinguish drivers with similar urgency but different dynamics.

Method: PCT decomposes personas along Temporal Urgency (3 levels) and Ride Comfort (3 levels) into 9 personas, each with language descriptions and trajectories. PersonaDrive learns persona representations from language and generates persona-specific trajectories. Key components: Persona-Conditioned Anchor Transform (PCAT) to hierarchically reshape anchors along both axes; Persona-Conditioned Multi-Modal Fusion (PCMF) for BEV-level fusion. Training employs Hierarchical Guide Loss to enforce axis-aligned physical orderings and Axis-Decomposed Diversity Loss to prevent diagonal mode collapse.

Result: Experimental results show PersonaDrive consistently improves over baselines across multi-dimensional scenarios; code and PCT dataset are publicly available at the provided GitHub link.

Conclusion: The work enables controllable, language-grounded persona conditioning for trajectory prediction, offering a dataset and framework that can better capture diverse driving styles and user preferences.

Abstract: Although recent trajectory prediction and end-to-end autonomous driving methods improve robustness in urban environments, they still lack meaningful controllability. Existing benchmarks either provide no persona-conditioned annotations or support only a single urgency spectrum (i.e., emergency, normal, relaxed), which cannot distinguish personas that share the same urgency level but require different driving dynamics. To address this, we propose (i) the Persona-Conditioned Trajectory (PCT) dataset, which decomposes driving personas along two axes, Temporal Urgency and Ride Comfort, and combines three levels of each to form a grid of nine personas, each paired with natural-language descriptions and trajectories, and (ii) PersonaDrive, a framework that can learn driving personas from language and can generate persona-specific trajectories. PersonaDrive incorporates Persona-Conditioned Anchor Transform (PCAT), which hierarchically reshapes anchors along both axes, and Persona-Conditioned Multi-Modal Fusion (PCMF) for BEV-level persona fusion. Training is supervised by a Hierarchical Guide Loss enforcing axis-aligned physical orderings and an Axis-Decomposed Diversity Loss preventing diagonal mode collapse. Experimental results show that PersonaDrive consistently improves over the compared baselines across multi-dimensional scenarios. The code and PCT dataset are available at https://github.com/VisualAIKHU/PersonaDrive

</details>


### [66] [UC-VLM: Consistency-Driven Learning for AI-Generated Image Detection with Vision-Language Large Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15238)
*Lei Tan,Shuwei Li,Mohan Kankanhalli,Robby T. Tan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Unified multi-stage binary-supervised VLLM framework (UC-VLM) for AIGI detection; uses automatic instruction variants and shared binary labels to supervise both visual and language outputs; achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on GenImage and Chameleon datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Need to improve robustness and scalability of VLLM-based detectors for AI-generated image detection by focusing on low-level forensic cues while avoiding reliance on manual prompts or rationales.

Method: Multi-stage training with binary supervision: (i) automatically identify effective instruction variants; (ii) visual discrimination objective to emphasize non-semantic forensic cues; (iii) label-conditioned generation objective to supervise textual outputs with the binary label; same binary label reused across visual and language pathways; no human-written rationales or hand-crafted prompts.

Result: GenImage: 96.1% average accuracy, +4.6% over prior; Chameleon: 69.6% (ProGAN) / 77.9% (SDV1.4), +11.2% / +15.3% over best baselines.

Conclusion: A unified, binary-supervised framework that leverages automatically optimized instructions to train both the visual and language components, reducing prompt sensitivity and improving AIGI detection performance across diverse datasets.

Abstract: Vision-Language Large Models (VLLMs) are promising for AI-generated image (AIGI) detection because they can produce both a prediction and a natural-language output. However, most existing VLLM-based detectors primarily fine-tune the language side while giving limited attention to low-level visual forensic cues. They also often depend on manually crafted prompts or human-annotated rationales, which limits scalability.We present UC-VLM, a unified multi-stage framework for AIGI detection that relies solely on binary supervision. UC-VLM first identifies effective instruction variants automatically. It then reuses the same binary label within a multi-stage training framework: (i) a visual discrimination objective that strengthens sensitivity to non-semantic forensic cues, and (ii) a label-conditioned generation objective that uses the binary label to supervise textual outputs. This design turns weak binary supervision into a shared supervision signal for both the visual pathway and the language output. Our key novelty is a unified multi-stage binary-supervised framework that consistently reuses the same authenticity labels for visual adaptation and label-conditioned text generation, while leveraging automatically optimized instructions to reduce prompt sensitivity without requiring human-written rationales or hand-crafted prompts.Experiments show that UC-VLM achieves 96.1% average accuracy on GenImage, exceeding the strongest prior result by 4.6%, and obtains 69.6% / 77.9% accuracy on Chameleon under ProGAN / SDV1.4 training, surpassing the best baseline by 11.2% / 15.3%, respectively.

</details>


### [67] [CG-GLORE: A Conjugate Gradient-Based Global-Local Regularization Network for Sparse-View CT Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15246)
*Tran Xuan Hieu Le,Doanh C. Bui,Vu Trung Duong Le,Hoai Luan Pham,Khang Nguyen,Mai K. Nguyen,Tu Bao Ho,Yasuhiko Nakashima*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CG-GLORE proposes a second-order-inspired unrolled framework for sparse-view CT that uses a CG-solved linear system with a Hessian surrogate for the data term and a Global-Local Regularization Network (GLORE) combining local convolutional features with Nyström-based long-range attention; it achieves strong quantitative results and stable convergence on sparse-view CT datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Sparse-view CT yields ill-posed inversions with streak artifacts; existing deep methods often rely on first-order updates or large networks and can struggle under ill-conditioning. A second-order-inspired approach aims to better exploit data fidelity curvature while maintaining a compact learned prior.

Method: Unrolled CG-GLORE uses a conjugate gradient (CG) solve of a linear system at each stage based on a structured Hessian surrogate that preserves data-fidelity curvature; the learned regularization is approximated by an identity to emulate a second-order update. The GLORE module combines convolutional local feature extraction with a Long-Range Dependency Representation using sparse patchification and Nyström attention to capture non-local anatomical structure with manageable complexity.

Result: On AAPM and DeepLesion datasets across multiple sparse-view and noise settings, CG-GLORE yields strong quantitative performance, stable convergence, lower noise power, and improved visual fidelity compared with representative reconstruction methods.

Conclusion: The framework demonstrates that second-order-inspired unrolling with a compact, effective prior can improve reconstruction quality and stability in ill-posed sparse-view CT, by balancing the curvature of data fidelity with learned priors through a CG-based optimization and a non-local-aware regularizer.

Abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reduces radiation dose by acquiring fewer projection views, but the resulting inverse problem is highly ill-posed and often produces severe streak artifacts. Existing deep reconstruction methods have achieved promising performance, yet many rely on first-order updates or large regularization networks, which can be less effective in ill-conditioned settings. We propose \textbf{CG-GLORE}, a compact deep unrolling framework inspired by second-order optimization for sparse-view CT reconstruction. Each unrolled stage uses a CG-solved linear system based on a structured Hessian surrogate: it retains the physics-induced curvature of the data-fidelity term while using an identity approximation for the learned regularization term. Thus, the method is second-order-inspired rather than an exact Newton method for the full learned objective. To model image priors, we design a Global-Local Regularization Network (GLORE), which combines convolutional local feature extraction with a Long-Range Dependency Representation module based on sparse patchification and Nyström attention. This design captures anatomical details and non-local dependencies while maintaining practical complexity. Experiments on AAPM and DeepLesion under multiple sparse-view and noise settings show that CG-GLORE achieves strong quantitative performance, stable convergence, lower noise power, and improved visual fidelity compared with representative reconstruction methods.

</details>


### [68] [Robust structure from motion for aerial-ground images via detector-free feature matching and multi-view track refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15251)
*San Jiang,Hui Wang,Xing Zhang,Zhongwen Hu,Zhijun Wang,Ruisheng Wang,Wanshou Jiang,Qingquan Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A rotation-robust, detector-free matching network with multi-view track refinement improves incremental Structure from Motion (ISfM) for aerial-ground imagery, outperforming LoFTR in pose robustness and reconstruction precision.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Robust feature matching under severe viewpoint, scale, and rotation variations is critical for accurate Integrated 3D reconstruction from aerial-ground images; existing detectors/matchers struggle with rotation and long-range dependencies.

Method: Four modules: (1) OSS Block for rotation-aware feature extraction across eight directions; (2) multi-scale quadtree attention to build a hierarchical token pyramid with linear complexity; (3) bi-directional symmetric coarse-to-fine matching with dual-direction Softmax under mutual NN constraints and sub-pixel offset regression via MLP; (4) multi-view track refinement using an indexing structure to link sub-tracks to a high-confidence anchor, ensuring repeatability in ISfM.

Result: On real aerial-ground datasets, AUC at 5° pose error improves by 93.9% over LoFTR; achieves the highest precision in ISfM reconstruction with accuracy gains of 27.6%–32.7%.

Conclusion: The proposed rotation-robust detector-free matching framework with multi-view track refinement delivers reliable, high-precision integrated 3D reconstructions for aerial-ground imagery, accommodating challenging rotations and viewpoint changes.

Abstract: Integrated 3D reconstruction from aerial-ground images is essential for generating high-precision urban 3D models, yet severe variations in viewpoint, scale, and rotation make robust feature matching highly challenging. To address these limitations, this study introduces a rotation-robust detector-free matching network coupled with multi-view track refinement for incremental Structure from Motion (ISfM). The proposed workflow features four key modules. First, rotation-aware feature extraction replaces traditional convolutions with an Omnidirectional State Space Block (OSS Block) that selectively scans across eight symmetrical directions to model long-range spatial dependencies and synthesize rotation-invariant feature maps. Second, multi-scale attention transformation utilizes quadtree attention to build a hierarchical token pyramid that isolates high-association token regions and discards irrelevant areas, capturing long-range context with linear computational complexity. Third, bi-directional feature matching executes a symmetric coarse-to-fine matching scheme where coarse alignment computes dual-direction Softmax confidence matrices under mutual nearest neighbor constraints, and fine alignment uses a multi-layer perceptron to regress sub-pixel coordinate offsets. Finally, multi-view track refinement employs an integrated indexing structure to evaluate localized spatial proximity and link disjoint sub-tracks to the highest-confidence anchor point, ensuring stable feature repeatability across the ISfM pipeline. By using real aerial-ground datasets, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves AUC at 5° pose error by 93.9% compared with LoFTR and achieves the highest precision in ISfM reconstruction, with the improved accuracy ranging from 27.6% to 32.7%. The proposed method provides a reliable solution for integrated 3D reconstruction of aerial-ground images.

</details>


### [69] [UAV Video Deblurring via Motion-Aware Diffusion: A Path to Robust Target Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15259)
*Zhiqiang Hu,Shouren Huang,Masatoshi Ishikawa*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Efficient UAV video deblurring framework using adaptive latent scale and multi-frame alignment with learnable gating, yielding improved deblurring and target detection on real UAV benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: UAV video capture experiences severe motion blur due to rapid maneuvers, vibrations, and panning, which degrades perception tasks; a computationally efficient deblurring solution is needed to boost downstream tasks like target detection.

Method: Introduce Adaptive Latent Scale Selector to adjust latent-space resolution based on motion intensity for efficiency and detail preservation. Use Multi-Frame Alignment and Learnable Gating to warp and gate preceding frames, fusing only relevant temporal information and suppressing misaligned/uninformative features for temporal consistency.

Result: The approach recovers sharp details from UAV video and, on real UAV benchmarks, achieves superior deblurring performance and significantly improves target detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency.

Conclusion: The proposed adaptive, temporally-aware deblurring framework enhances UAV video quality and downstream detection tasks, supporting robust, real-time aerial vision applications.

Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) play a crucial role in various scenarios ranging from disaster response to traffic surveillance. However, aerial video footage often suffers from severe motion blur due to rapid flight maneuvers, vibrations, and camera panning, which can significantly degrade downstream tasks such as target detection. Our goal is to explore a computationally-efficient and effective video deblurring approach to enhance UAV target detection performance. To reduce computational cost, we first propose an Adaptive Latent Scale Selector that dynamically adjusts the latent space resolution according to the intensity of UAV motion, thus balancing detail preservation with inference efficiency. To ensure temporal consistency, we introduce a Multi-Frame Alignment and Learnable Gating module to warp and gate the preceding frames, allowing the model to fuse only relevant temporal information and suppress misaligned or uninformative features. Our method can effectively recover sharp details from the UAV video stream. Extensive experiments on real UAV benchmarks demonstrate that our method not only yields superior deblurring performance but also significantly boosts target detection accuracy, making it highly applicable to robust aerial vision tasks.

</details>


### [70] [VGGT-Align: Bridging Local Reconstruction and Global Consistency for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15260)
*Wei Zhang,Yihang Wu,Songhua Li,Qi Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SGIA anchors per-chunk scale in long-sequence 3D reconstruction by exploiting cross-chunk geometric invariants, converting Sim(3) drift to rigid motion misalignment, and applying light test-time adaptation; achieves state-of-the-art results without offline retraining.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Global geometric consistency in long sequences is compromised by unconstrained scale drift in chunk-based Sim(3) alignment; invariant environmental geometry offers a stable basis to constrain scale across chunks.

Method: Extract dominant geometric invariants from each chunk’s predicted point cloud via coarse-to-fine robust estimation; use cross-chunk consistency to impose scale constraints independent of point-cloud registration; degenerate 7-DoF Sim(3) into 6-DoF rigid-body transformation by anchoring scale through invariants. Introduce lightweight test-time adaptation that fine-tunes normalization-layer parameters with multi-objective self-supervision to improve intra-chunk predictions across the sequence.

Result: Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple long-sequence benchmarks; absolute trajectory error reduced by up to 32%; improved trajectory stability and reconstruction quality.

Conclusion: Plug-and-play framework requiring no offline retraining; scalable and practical for long-sequence 3D reconstruction; code released for reproducibility.

Abstract: Maintaining global geometric consistency is a central challenge in long-sequence 3D reconstruction, with scale drift being the most critical failure mode. In chunk-based inference pipelines, the scale degree of freedom in sequential Sim(3) alignment is left unconstrained, causing estimation errors to compound multiplicatively and distort global trajectories and point cloud geometry. We present a scale-consistency enhancement framework built on a key insight: in structured environments such as driving scenes, geometric quantities arising from environmental regularity remain inherently invariant across temporal segments, and discrepancies in their per-chunk measurements directly expose inter-chunk scale drift. We propose Scene Geometric Invariant Anchoring (SGIA), which extracts dominant geometric invariants from each chunk's predicted point cloud via coarse-to-fine robust estimation and exploits their cross-chunk consistency to establish scale constraints independent of point cloud registration, explicitly degenerating 7-DoF Sim(3) alignment into 6-DoF rigid-body transformation and severing chain-wise scale error propagation at its source. We further introduce a lightweight test-time adaptation strategy that fine-tunes only normalization-layer parameters via multi-objective self-supervision, progressively improving intra-chunk predictions along the sequence. Both modules are plug-and-play and require no offline retraining. Experiments on multiple long-sequence benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, reducing absolute trajectory error by up to 32% with significant gains in trajectory stability and reconstruction quality. Code: https://github.com/WZ-CS/VGGT-Align

</details>


### [71] [Boundary-Aligned Contribution Routing for Robust Optical--SAR Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15261)
*Haifa Zhang,Yijing Wang,Haoyu Wang,Zheng Li,Zhiqiang Zuo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes fusion-boundary-aligned routing to adaptively weight optical and SAR modalities for detection, using task-conditioned routers that operate before cross-modal fusion, improving robustness to missing/corrupted modalities without extra supervision.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Mitigate negative cross-modal transfer due to imperfect spatial/temporal/semantic alignment in optical–SAR fusion; leverage task-utility perspective to route modality contributions under detection supervision only.

Method: Introduce two routers: (i) a Feature Router for shallow-interaction architectures that modulates inputs via cross-conditioned, group-addressable gating near the input; (ii) a Dual-Statistic Semantic Router for dual-backbone models that uses modality-specific average and max statistics to predict stream-level modality weights before late semantic fusion. Routers require no explicit utility labels or distillation.

Result: On M4-SAR and SpaceNet6-OTD, routing improves full-input mAP50 by 0.5–5.9 points, missing-modality mAP50 by 7.6–41.6 points, reduces negative-transfer rate by up to 12.7 percentage points; Spearman correlation between router weights and modality-utility 0.45–0.66.

Conclusion: Task-utility guided routing enables effective, supervision-light fusion for optical–SAR object detection, enhancing robustness to missing/corrupted modalities and reducing negative transfer.

Abstract: Optical imagery provides rich appearance cues, whereas synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers observations that are less sensitive to illumination and weather, making optical--SAR fusion attractive for remote-sensing object detection. However, the presence of multiple modalities does not guarantee beneficial fusion: imperfect spatial, temporal, and semantic correspondence can make an otherwise intact stream conditionally harmful and induce negative cross-modal transfer. We handle this issue through a model-specific task-utility perspective and learn task-conditioned contribution routing using detection supervision alone. The proposed fusion-boundary-aligned routing regulates each modality's contribution before the first learned cross-modal feature-value mixing operation. For architectures with frequent shallow interaction, a Feature Router performs cross-conditioned, group-addressable modulation near the input; for dual-backbone architectures, a Dual-Statistic Semantic Router predicts stream-level contribution weights from modality-specific average and maximum statistics before late semantic fusion. The routers require no explicit utility supervision, quality labels, reconstruction, or distillation. Experiments on M4-SAR and SpaceNet6-OTD cover nominal full inputs, controlled correspondence shifts, missing modalities, and four nonzero modality-corruption scenarios. Across the reported clean-training controls, routing improves full-input $\text{mAP}_{50}$ by 0.5--5.9 points. Relative to the corresponding modality-dropout baselines, it raises missing-modality $\text{mAP}_{50}$ by 7.6--41.6 points and reduces the negative-transfer rate by up to 12.7 percentage points. Spearman correlations between the learned routing weights and model-specific leave-one-modality-out utility range from 0.45 to 0.66, supporting the task-utility interpretation of the routing coefficients.

</details>


### [72] [On the Adversarial Robustness of Remote Sensing Semantic Change Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15267)
*Weikang Yu,Yonghao Xu,Pedram Ghamisi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A task-specific robustness framework for semantic change detection (SCD) shows cross-temporal adversarial perturbations can severely degrade final semantic-change predictions even when locality of changes remains stable; robustness hinges on the whole bitemporal prediction pathway, not individual branches, and a structured evaluation protocol is proposed with code released.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: SCD couples two temporal inputs and performs timestamp-wise semantic predictions, creating adversarial dependencies not captured by standard robustness tests. There is a need for a dedicated evaluation framework to dissect vulnerabilities across inputs, timestamps, and output predictions.

Method: Introduce a task-specific robustness evaluation framework that decouples output-side attack objectives from input-side temporal perturbation access. Systematically assess component-level and temporal vulnerabilities using four datasets and six models (CNNs, Transformers, state-space). Analyze single- and dual-timestamp perturbations, multiple attack strategies, and cross-architecture transferability.

Result: Final semantic-change predictions are highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, even when binary change localization is stable. Perturbations tied to one timestamp can propagate to the other timestamp’s prediction. Vulnerabilities persist across architecture families; cross-model transfer is weaker than white-box attacks. The work emphasizes evaluating robustness along the full bitemporal pathway and provides a structured protocol, with code available.

Conclusion: Robustness in SCD depends on the complete bitemporal prediction pipeline rather than isolated components. The paper offers a principled evaluation framework for coupled bitemporal image analysis and highlights the need for defenses that consider cross-temporal propagation.

Abstract: Semantic change detection (SCD) is a bitemporal dense-prediction task that jointly identifies changed regions and their semantic states before and after change. Unlike single-image segmentation or binary change detection, SCD couples two temporal inputs with timestamp-wise semantic prediction, change localization, and final semantic-change decoding, creating adversarial dependencies that are not captured by conventional robustness protocols. We present a task-specific evaluation framework that separates output-side attack objectives from input-side temporal perturbation access, enabling systematic analysis of component vulnerability and cross-temporal propagation. Experiments on four datasets and six representative CNN-, Transformer-, and state-space-based models evaluate component-level and temporal objectives, single- and dual-timestamp perturbations, multiple attack methods, and cross-architecture transferability. The results show that final semantic-change predictions can be severely corrupted even when binary change localization remains comparatively stable, and that perturbations or attack objectives associated with one timestamp can propagate to the prediction of the other. These behaviors occur across different architecture families, while direct cross-model transfer remains considerably weaker than white-box attacks. The study demonstrates that adversarial robustness in SCD depends on the complete bitemporal prediction pathway rather than on an individual branch or backbone family, and provides a structured protocol for evaluating robustness in coupled bitemporal image analysis. Code is available at https://github.com/EricYu97/AdvSCD.

</details>


### [73] [Memory-Bounded Continuation of Greedy Sampling for Continual Anomaly Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15277)
*Yoon Gyo Jung,Jaewoo Park,Kuan-Chuan Peng,Seongdeok Bang,Octavia Camps*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ContCore: a fixed-memory, greedy-continued coreset method for continual anomaly detection that preserves representativeness under memory constraints, with theoretical guarantees and strong empirical performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the need for a fixed-size coreset in sequential tasks to enable reliable anomaly detection, avoiding unbounded memory growth and catastrophic forgetting. Observes that repeatedly applying greedy sampling to the already sampled set can retain representativeness under strict memory limits.

Method: Construct a greedy-continued coreset by expanding on new task features via greedy selection, then consolidate greedily to enforce a fixed memory budget. At each task, discard data as needed to maintain memory size, and show that the resulting coreset approximates the oracle coreset within a bounded gap.

Result: Theoretically bound the approximation gap to the oracle coreset. Empirically achieve state-of-the-art performance across 11 task schedules on MVTecAD and VisA, and remain effective in online continual anomaly detection settings where prior methods degrade.

Conclusion: ContCore provides fixed-memory management with theoretical guarantees and superior empirical performance, outperforming neural methods prone to forgetting and naive unbounded coreset accumulation; code available at the provided repository.

Abstract: Greedy sampling produces a compact yet representative summary of normal data, which is essential for reliable anomaly detection that relies on measuring distance from normality. For continual anomaly detection where tasks arrive sequentially, extending greedy sampling is straightforward with unbounded memory through coreset accumulation. However, practical deployment requires fixed memory where the coreset size remains constant regardless of task count. We observe that continued greedy sampling, which iteratively applies greedy selection over previously greedy-sampled sets, effectively preserves representativeness under strict memory limits. Despite discarding data at each step to satisfy the memory constraint, coreset quality degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically, enabling reliable anomaly detection across the tasks. We provide theoretical justification by showing that resulting greedy-continued coreset approximates the oracle coreset within a bounded gap. We instantiate this principle in ContCore, which constructs a greedy-continued coreset through greedy expansion on new task features followed by greedy consolidation to enforce the memory budget. Unlike neural methods susceptible to catastrophic forgetting or naive coreset accumulation requiring unbounded memory, ContCore maintains fixed memory with theoretical guarantees. Empirically, ContCore achieves state-of-the-art performance across 11 task schedules on MVTecAD and VisA, and extends effectively to online continual AD settings where prior methods degrade significantly.
