Blind re-captioning plus a general LLM judge improves results but is unstable, oscillating between 0% and 100% flagged depending on prompt phrasing. Replacing that judge with a small natural language inference model yields a stable, interpretable verifier that catches 79% of fabricated claims on adversarial false-premise questions while leaving true claims untouched. We release the full pipeline, evaluation harness, and implementations for both Apple Silicon and Colab. Code is available at https://github.com/yogesh-iitj/grounded-video-qa.

</details>


### [99] [X$^2$Localizer: Cross-grained Alignment for Progressive Cross-view Video Geo-localization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16658)
*Zichao Zeng,Weijia Fan,Yufan Chen,June Moh Goo,Junwei Zheng,Ruiping Liu,Kunyu Peng,Jiaming Zhang,Rainer Stiefelhagen,Jan Boehm*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes PCVG framework for deployment-aware cross-view video geo-localization with X^2Localizer and SWRL to enable online localization under partial observations; achieves comparable full-video performance with strong gains in early localization and robustness.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: CVG methods are constrained by fixed-length inputs and post-hoc refinement, hindering online/localization under partial/dynamic observations; need deployment-oriented evaluation protocol.

Method: Define Progressive Cross-view Video Geo-localization (PCVG). Introduce X^2Localizer for cross-grained alignment with global prefix-to-aerial retrieval and token-aggregated frame–aerial-tile matching under budget constraints; propose SWRL sliding-window re-localization to refresh candidate regions without reprocessing entire sequence.

Result: Preserves full-video performance with marginal gains (Recall@1 +0.1, Recall@10 +0.3); substantially improves early localization; in single-frame setting, gains +4.7 Recall@1 and +11.5 Recall@10 over SOTA; SWRL enables robust progressive localization under random-start and long-distance scenarios.

Conclusion: Demonstrates deployment-oriented CVG pipeline that balances online efficiency with localization accuracy, improving robustness and applicability to real-world, partial-observation scenarios.

Abstract: Cross-view Video Geo-localization (CVG) aims to localize ground-view videos by retrieving their corresponding geo-tagged aerial images. However, CVG approaches rely on fixed-length inputs and post-hoc refinement, hindering online-oriented localization under partial or dynamic observations. In this work, we formulate Progressive Cross-view Video Geo-localization (PCVG) as a deployment-oriented extension and evaluation protocol of CVG, enabling localization under varying temporal budgets, prefix-based inference, random-start evaluation, and long-range localization with interruptions. To explore PCVG, we introduce X$^2$Localizer, a cross-grained alignment framework that jointly supervises global prefix-to-aerial retrieval and token-aggregated frame--aerial-tile matching with a budget-dependent asymmetric objective. Furthermore, we introduce a Sliding-Window Re-Localization (SWRL) strategy that dynamically refreshes candidate regions for failure recovery and long-range deployment without full-sequence reprocessing. Extensive experiments show that X$^2$Localizer preserves conventional full-video performance, with marginal gains of +0.1 Recall@1 and +0.3 Recall@10, while substantially improving early localization. In the challenging single-frame setting, X$^2$Localizer improves coarse retrieval by +4.7 Recall@1 and +11.5 Recall@10 over the previous state-of-the-art method. With SWRL, our approach further enables robust progressive localization under random-start and long-distance scenarios, narrowing the gap between benchmark evaluation and real-world deployment.

</details>


### [100] [PoseAdapter: Dual-Stream 2.5D Controllable Image Generation for Complex Multi-Object Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15583)
*Yufeng Chi,Huimin Ma,Fan Gao,Zhice Niu,Keqin Li,Jianmin Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PoseAdapter enables high-fidelity 2.5D controllable image generation in T2I diffusion models by using per-object captions, 2D bounding boxes, and 3D angles, with a Context-Aware Dual-Stream Representation to avoid attribute leakage, and introduces OrientLayout dataset; it outperforms baselines on spatial/orientational accuracy and multi-object fidelity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Accurate spatial and orientational control in multi-object scenes is difficult; dense 3D maps are costly and prone to leakage/artifacts; need architectures that preserve inter-object relations while isolating instances.

Method: Propose PoseAdapter: condition layout using per-object captions, 2D boxes, and 3D angles; Context-Aware Dual-Stream Representation with local object tokens and relation-enriched scene tokens injected into MM-DiT via parallel masked/unmasked pathways; dataset OrientLayout with 2.5D annotations and decoupled semantics.

Result: Experiments show superior performance versus state-of-the-art baselines in spatial accuracy, orientational precision, and multi-object visual fidelity.

Conclusion: PoseAdapter provides a scalable, effective approach for 2.5D controllable generation; OrientLayout supports evaluation and learning; code and data will be released.

Abstract: While Text-to-Image (T2I) diffusion models have achieved remarkable success, precise spatial and orientational control in multi-object scenes remains a persistent challenge. Existing methods either rely on computationally expensive dense 3D maps or suffer from severe attribute leakage and "cut-and-paste" artifacts. To address these limitations, we propose PoseAdapter, a lightweight framework for high-fidelity 2.5D controllable image generation. Instead of dense spatial maps, it establishes precise spatial-angular anchors using an efficient condition layout: individual object captions, 2D bounding boxes, and 3D angles. To resolve the generative trade-off between strict instance isolation and global coherence, we introduce a Context-Aware Dual-Stream Representation. By injecting local object tokens and relation-enriched scene tokens into the visual stream of modern MM-DiT architectures via parallel masked and unmasked pathways, PoseAdapter eliminates attribute leakage while preserving natural inter-object relationships and scene-level coherence. To support this paradigm, we construct OrientLayout, a high-quality dataset featuring standardized 2.5D annotations and instance-level decoupled semantics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PoseAdapter outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in spatial accuracy, orientational precision, and multi-object visual fidelity. Code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/cyf23/PoseAdapter.

</details>


### [101] [AlloEgo-VLM: Disambiguating Allocentric and Egocentric Reference Frames in Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15605)
*Kuan-Lin Chen,Tzu-Ti Wei,Chao-Chi Liao,Yu-Chee Tseng,Jen-Jee Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces AlloEgo-View dataset and AlloEgo-VLM to disambiguate allocentric and egocentric spatial frames for VLMs, validated on an embodied robot.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Spatial descriptions often omit reference frames, causing semantic ambiguity. This leads to errors in VLMs and embodied AI; current models lack sufficient training on reference frames and object orientations.

Method: Construct AlloEgo-View, a dataset of image-query-view triplets with allocentric and egocentric annotations, and develop AlloEgo-VLM via supervised fine-tuning to resolve frame ambiguity. Use a structured spatial representation (scene details, reference/target objects, orientations, reference frames, view types) and integrate into existing VLMs. Validate on an embodied robotic platform in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for open-ended object search tasks.

Result: Experiments show current VLMs struggle with view-specific (allocentric vs. egocentric) queries, while AlloEgo-VLM demonstrates strong disambiguation capability.

Conclusion: Frame-aware disambiguation for spatial relations is feasible and beneficial for embodied AI; the AlloEgo framework can be integrated into existing VLMs to improve reliability in view-dependent reasoning.

Abstract: This study investigates the challenge of ambiguity faced by Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in understanding spatial semantics. Spatial cognition, shaped by cognitive psychology, spatial science, and cultural context, often assigns directionality to objects. However, natural language descriptions of spatial relations frequently omit explicit reference frames, leading to semantic ambiguity and potentially serious errors for embodied AI robots. Existing VLMs, due to insufficient training on reference frames and object orientations, often produce inconsistent responses. To address this issue, we construct a new dataset, AlloEgo-View, comprising (image, query, view-specific answer) triplets that capture key object relations from both allocentric and egocentric perspectives. The view-specific descriptions follow a structured spatial representation that annotate detailed scene descriptions, reference and target objects, their orientations, reference frames, and view types. Building on AlloEgo-View, we develop AlloEgo-VLM, a framework to disambiguate allocentric and egocentric reference frames, even under ambiguous queries, and to be easily integrated into existing VLMs via supervised fine-tuning. Furthermore, we deploy our framework onto an embodied robotic platform within NVIDIA Isaac Sim to validate its real-world feasibility in open-ended object searching tasks. Experiments highlight the limitations of current VLMs in handling view-specific queries and demonstrate the strong disambiguation ability of AlloEgo-VLM.

</details>


### [102] [EgoGazeLite: On-Device Egocentric Gaze Prediction for Token-Efficient Multimodal LLM Video Input](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15614)
*Matteo Stoiber,Niels Buus Lassen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A lightweight, on-device gaze predictor (EgoGazeLite) matches ground-truth gaze crops for egocentric video, enabling token-efficient MLLMs without eye-tracking hardware; it runs in real time on consumer hardware with 15.7M parameters and 6.71 GFLOPs.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Reduce token budget and processing cost in egocentric video understanding by predicting gaze without external eye-tracking hardware; enable software-only, on-device gaze-conditioned processing within smartphone constraints.

Method: A dual-process gaze predictor (EgoGazeLite) evaluated with two MLLMs, three automated metrics, and two LLM judges; compares predicted gaze crops against ground-truth gaze crops to demonstrate equivalence across ten cases; achieves end-to-end real-time gaze-and-crop on consumer accelerators.

Result: Predicted gaze crops show no significant difference from ground-truth crops; equivalence confirmed in all ten cases; on-device pipeline runs at 21.6 ms/frame; model is 15.7M parameters with 6.71 GFLOPs.

Conclusion: Software-only gaze prediction suffices to enable token-efficient, gaze-conditioned egocentric video understanding with MLLMs, removing the need for eye-tracking hardware.

Abstract: The use of multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) for egocentric video understanding with wearable devices is constrained by the token budget. Memory and compute cost scale with the number of visual tokens, and high-resolution video quickly becomes expensive to transmit and process at scale. Prior work (GazeLLM) addresses this by cropping the video around the camera wearer's gaze. This reduces the number of visual tokens by about tenfold while maintaining or improving the quality of full-resolution descriptions. However, this compression strategy depends on dedicated eye-tracking hardware, which is unavailable on consumer smart glasses. Building a software-only substitute poses a joint constraint: the predictor must be accurate enough to preserve downstream description quality, yet light enough to run on-device, within the power and compute budget of a smartphone. We address this with EgoGazeLite, a lightweight dual-process gaze predictor for egocentric video. Across two MLLMs, three automated metrics, and two LLM judges, predicted-gaze crops show no significant difference from ground-truth-gaze crops. Equivalence is confirmed in all ten cases. EgoGazeLite achieves this at 15.7M parameters, 6.71 GFLOPs, and runs the full gaze-and-crop pipeline end-to-end in real time (21.6 ms/frame) on consumer accelerator hardware. Together, these results remove the need for eye-tracking hardware for token-efficient, gaze-conditioned egocentric video understanding with MLLMs.

</details>


### [103] [Hierarchical Adaptive Feature Refinement Network for VHR Remote Sensing Image Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15647)
*Shuaishuai Cao,Meng Tang,Shuwei Peng,Xuan Liu,Min Huang,Jie Chen,Jiacheng Niu,Yong Chen,Edore Akpokodje,Hui Lin*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: HAFR-Net is a progressive refinement framework for semantic segmentation of VHR remote sensing imagery that adaptively fuses hierarchical encoders, adds a frequency-aware residual adapter, and employs a tri-prior decoder to improve boundary and thin-structure accuracy, outperforming a matched UPerNet baseline on four datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Exploit multi-stage pretrained encoders by adaptively leveraging their hierarchical representations while avoiding aggressive feature perturbations and providing stronger structural guidance for segmentation.

Method: HG-SAF predicts dense stage weights conditioned on local feature variation to guide hierarchical fusion. FRA injects frequency information via a bounded, zero-initialized residual branch, keeping the fused representation reference. CATP regularizes predictions using boundary, objectness, and training-derived class-relations cues. Training uses matched Swin-B backbone and single-scale inference.

Result: On ISPRS Vaihingen, Potsdam, LoveDA, and OpenEarthMap, HAFR-Net achieves mIoU of 84.12%, 87.86%, 55.17%, and 67.70% respectively, surpassing the matched UPerNet baseline by 0.55, 0.95, 1.55, and 1.84 percentage points.

Conclusion: HAFR-Net demonstrates consistent spatial reweighting beyond content-only routing, improved boundary and thin-structure accuracy compared to spatial/spectral alternatives, and reduced confusion on predefined class pairs, validating hierarchical refinement over a monolithic decoder.

Abstract: Semantic segmentation of very-high-resolution (VHR) remote sensing imagery increasingly benefits from strong pretrained hierarchical encoders, yet exploiting their multi-stage representations remains difficult. Nearby regions demand different balances between fine detail and semantic context, aggressive task-specific transformations perturb useful pretrained features, and conventional semantic supervision provides limited structural guidance. We present HAFR-Net, a progressive refinement framework that adaptively organizes and conservatively refines hierarchical representations instead of replacing them with a monolithic decoder transformation. Heterogeneity-Guided Stage-Adaptive Fusion (HG-SAF) predicts dense stage weights conditioned on local feature variation. A Frequency-Residual Adapter (FRA) then injects frequency information through a bounded, zero-initialized residual branch that keeps the fused representation as its reference. A Confusion-Aware Tri-Prior Decoder (CATP) finally regularizes the prediction with boundary, objectness, and training-derived class-relation cues. Under a matched Swin-B training and single-scale inference protocol, HAFR-Net attains 84.12%, 87.86%, 55.17%, and 67.70% mIoU on ISPRS Vaihingen, ISPRS Potsdam, LoveDA, and OpenEarthMap, improving the matched UPerNet baseline by 0.55, 0.95, 1.55, and 1.84 percentage points, respectively. Controlled analyses further show consistent spatial reweighting beyond content-only routing, improved boundary and thin-structure accuracy over matched spatial and spectral alternatives, and reduced confusion on pre-declared class pairs.

</details>


### [104] [Gaussian-JEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for 3D Gaussian Splats](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15651)
*Bin Ren,Qi Ma,Yue Li,Zongyan Han,Yidi Li,Yuqian Fu,Rao Muhammad Anwer,Theo Gevers,Fahad Shahbaz Khan,Salman Khan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Gaussian-JEPA introduces latent prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by forecasting representations of held-out Gaussian token blocks from visible context, using an online encoder and EMA teacher, with projection targets and feature grounding; it avoids Gaussian-attribute reconstruction and yields robust, transferable features under resampling, partial observations, and shape completion, outperforming reconstruction pretraining.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Limitations of fixed-budget, reconstruction-based self-supervision for 3D Gaussian assets: supervision tied to a single observed realization and the need for an input-space decoder. Latent prediction offers a reconstruction-free objective to learn reusable 3D representations that can handle heterogeneous spatial support.

Method: Gaussian-JEPA: (i) online encoder processes visible context tokens; (ii) a shared exponential-moving-average (EMA) encoder provides stop-gradient features as multi-scale targets; (iii) complementary target projections and feature-space grounding enable latent supervision without reconstructing Gaussian attributes; (iv) train to predict representations of held-out Gaussian token blocks from context.

Result: Evaluations include Gaussian resampling, partial observations, and renderable shape completion, plus transfers to part segmentation and object classification. Gaussian-JEPA exhibits greater consistency across resampled inputs, preserves more instance information under partial observations, and yields stronger frozen features for completion compared with matched reconstruction pretraining; code available on project page.

Conclusion: Latent prediction with Gaussian-JEPA is an effective self-supervised objective for reusable 3D Gaussian representations, enabling robust, transferable features without reconstructing Gaussian attributes.

Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) represents 3D content with anisotropic primitives that jointly encode geometry and appearance. Fixed-budget encoders consume sampled observations of Gaussian assets, so the same object may be observed through different primitive realizations. Existing self-supervised methods mainly reconstruct masked Gaussian attributes, tying supervision to one sampled realization and requiring an input-space decoder. Latent prediction offers an alternative, but its application to Gaussian tokens requires targets that accommodate coupled attributes and heterogeneous spatial support. We introduce Gaussian-JEPA, which predicts representations of held-out Gaussian token blocks from visible context. An online encoder processes the context, while a shared exponential-moving-average encoder supplies stop-gradient features for multi-scale targets. Complementary target projections and feature-space grounding provide latent supervision without reconstructing Gaussian attributes. We evaluate the features under Gaussian resampling, partial observations, and renderable shape completion, together with transfer to part segmentation and object classification. Compared with matched reconstruction pretraining, Gaussian-JEPA is more consistent across resampled inputs, retains more instance information under partial observations, and provides stronger frozen features for Gaussian completion. These results support latent prediction as an effective objective for reusable 3D Gaussian representations. Code is on the project page (https://amazingren.github.io/Gaussian-JEPA/).

</details>


### [105] [BASeg: Boundary-Aware Remote Sensing Segmentation with Structural Penalties](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15683)
*Yuexi Song,Kailai Sun,Zhuoyu Wang,Mingyi He,Paul Pu Liang,Shenhao Wang,Jinhua Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes Mahalanobis-Angle Boundary Loss (MABL) to enhance boundary/shape consistency in remote-sensing segmentation; introduces BASeg with GSM and CFM, plus a global GCD-25k dataset; reports consistent mIoU gains up to 2.8% across benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current methods struggle with fine-grained object boundaries and diverse city morphology; segmentation on generative images remains underexplored; need boundary-aware, structure-preserving losses and architectures capable of long-range context and local detail.

Method: Develop MABL: weighting by Mahalanobis distance to emphasize structurally important regions and an angle-aware penalty to align boundary orientation. Integrate MABL into diverse architectures. Build BASeg framework with a Global Visual State Space (GSM) module for long-range context and a Cross-Feature Fusion (CFM) module for fusing global/local information. Create GCD-25k, a 10-city global benchmark for building/road segmentation. Evaluate on four remote-sensing benchmarks.

Result: BASeg achieves up to 2.8% mIoU improvement and yields sharper, more accurate object boundaries across diverse scenes; incorporating MABL into multiple architectures yields robust performance gains across datasets.

Conclusion: MABL offers a robust, broadly applicable boundary-aware loss; BASeg with GSM/CFM delivers improved segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity; the GCD-25k dataset enables evaluation over diverse city morphologies and supports future research.

Abstract: Semantic segmentation is a core computer vision task in the remote sensing field, accelerating advancements in ur- ban development, agriculture, ecology, water resources, and environmental monitoring. However, recent methods usually struggle to capture fine-grained object features and bound- ary details. Besides, current widely used datasets often lack city morphology diversity and segmentation on generative im- ages remains largely unexplored. To address these issues, we propose a Mahalanobis-Angle Boundary Loss (MABL) that explicitly enhances boundary and shape consistency. MABL jointly models structural importance and boundary orientation through Mahalanobis distance-based weighting and angle- aware penalty. It can be readily integrated into diverse seg- mentation architectures and consistently improves their accu- racy. Built upon MABL, we introduce BASeg, a boundary- aware remote sensing segmentation framework with Struc- tural Penalties. BASeg integrates a Global Visual State Space module (GSM) with a Cross-Feature Fusion module (CFM) to capture both long-range contextual dependencies and fine- grained local details. Additionally, we establish a global 10- city benchmark dataset (GCD-25k) to facilitate accurate build- ing and road segmentation. Extensive experiments on four remote-sensing benchmarks demonstrate that BASeg consis- tently outperforms existing methods, achieving up to a 2.8% improvement in mIoU while producing more accurate object boundary segmentation across diverse scenes. Moreover, integrating MABL into multiple existing segmentation archi- tectures consistently improves performance across datasets, demonstrating its robustness and broad applicability.

</details>


### [106] [Counterfactual Sensitivity Is Not Repairability: Auditing Replay Probes for Video Evidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15685)
*Rama AlHamidi,Rasul Khanbayov,Erchin Serpedin,Hasan Kurban*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CARVE is a black-box counterfactual probe that tests whether visually retrieved evidence causally influences answers in tool-using video agents by comparing SHAM and DESTROY replays; DESTROY more often changes answers, indicating a routing signal rather than direct grounding, with modest accuracy gains on LVBench.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Assess causal reliance on retrieved visual evidence and grounding in video QA, using a black-box, replay-based counterfactual probe to quantify how destroying retrieved semantic content affects answers.

Method: Three independent k=3 replays on a frozen VideoExplorer-style agent. Compare two replay conditions: SHAM (matched pipeline with intact frames) and DESTROY (destroyed semantic content in retrieved frames). Measure answer changes, aggregate across runs, vary replay budget k (3→10), assess impact on question-level stability and routing policy, evaluate on LVBench. Report accuracy gains and correlation with temporal coverage.

Result: DESTROY changes the answer 29.3 percentage points more often than SHAM across runs, indicating a strong aggregate effect. At k=3, CARVE selects 538 of 1,258 LVBench questions and improves accuracy by 3.26 points, with higher fallback yield than most matched random subsets. Increasing k to 10 reduces ties but weakens the original zero-threshold routing policy. The score has only a weak association with annotated temporal coverage, suggesting CARVE functions as a routing signal rather than a direct grounding classifier.

Conclusion: CARVE provides a reproducible, black-box routing signal that assesses reliance on retrieved frames without serving as an explicit grounding classifier. The approach yields measurable, robust effects across runs and offers a practical tool for probing grounding in video agents. Implementation is available at the linked GitHub repository.

Abstract: Tool-using video agents retrieve visual evidence before answering, but the final answer is not forced to depend on what was retrieved. The natural black box test is counterfactual: destroy the semantic content of the frames the agent retrieved and check whether the answer changes, against a matched sham that re-executes the identical pipeline on those same frames. We introduce CARVE, a black-box counterfactual probe that compares answer changes under matched SHAM and DESTROY replays. Across three independent k=3 runs on a frozen VideoExplorer-style agent, DESTROY changes the answer 29.3 percentage points more often than SHAM, yielding a large and reproducible aggregate effect. Question-level scores are less stable, and increasing the replay budget from k=3 to k=10 reduces ties but weakens the original zero-threshold routing policy. At k=3, CARVE selects 538 of 1,258 LVBench questions and improves accuracy by 3.26 points, with higher fallback yield than most matched random subsets. The score shows only a weak association with annotated temporal coverage, so CARVE is best understood as a routing signal rather than a direct grounding classifier. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/CARVE.

</details>


### [107] [Training-Free Long-Term Multi-Object Tracking for Sports Video Analytics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15688)
*Tomasz Stanczyk,Seongro Yoon,Francois Bremond*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A training-free, lightweight long-term multi-object tracking framework (McByte++) that boosts efficiency and identity preservation via mask propagation, camera motion compensation, and online re-ID, outperforming the original McByte on SoccerNet-tracking and SportsMOT with substantial ID metrics gains and faster inference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Tackle long-term MOT in sports under occlusion, rapid camera motion, and repeated appearances while avoiding detector retraining or dataset-specific tuning.

Method: A unified training-free tracking-by-detection pipeline integrating (i) lightweight mask propagation, (ii) conditional camera motion compensation, and (iii) online re-identification; replaces heavy segmentation components and optimizes motion modeling for significant speedups; compatible with online operation and benefits further from offline global association.

Result: On SoccerNet-tracking and SportsMOT, McByte++ achieves up to +3.0 HOTA and +6.1 IDF1 improvements over the original McByte in online settings, with further gains when combined with offline global association; replaces heavy components yields up to an order-of-magnitude speed increase; all results without detector retraining or dataset-specific tuning.

Conclusion: McByte++ substantially improves both accuracy (identity preservation) and efficiency relative to McByte, enabling practical long-term MOT in sports without retraining, with code to be released.

Abstract: Long-term multi-object tracking in sports remains challenging due to frequent occlusions, rapid camera motion, and repeated player reappearances. We introduce McByte++, a training-free tracking-by-detection framework that integrates lightweight mask propagation, conditional camera motion compensation, and online re-identification within a unified pipeline. Compared to its predecessor, McByte++ substantially improves runtime efficiency while enhancing identity preservation. On SoccerNet-tracking and SportsMOT benchmarks, McByte++ achieves up to +3.0 HOTA and +6.1 IDF1 improvements over the original McByte in the online setting, with further gains when combined with offline global association. Replacing heavy segmentation components and optimizing motion modeling yields up to an order-of-magnitude speed increase. All results are obtained without detector retraining or dataset-specific tuning. Code will be made available at https://github.com/tstanczyk95/McBytePlusPlus.

</details>


### [108] [ConceptFormer: Learning Adaptive Latent Concepts for Query-Document Alignment in Visual Document Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15698)
*Peng Chunyi,Xu Zhipeng,Yan Yukun,Liu Zhenghao,Yu Shi,Mei Sen,Sun Yubo,Zhang Yongheng,Zhou Jie,Gu Yu,Yu Ge,Sun Maosong*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ConceptFormer introduces latent concept tokens as query-conditioned intermediaries to bridge localized visual evidence and semantic relevance for visual document retrieval, avoiding textual intermediates or raw visual annotations. It yields sizable gains on average NDCG@10 across benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current supervision signals—textual descriptions or localized visual regions—either miss complex visual structures or misrepresent underlying evidence. A latent, query-conditioned representation can capture both fine-grained cues and global document-level visual structures.

Method: Train with a strong vision–language model that dynamically determines the number of latent concept tokens. These continuous latent concepts act as an intermediate representation to align queries with documents, guiding embedding space learning without relying on textual intermediates or raw visual annotations.

Result: Experiments across diverse benchmarks show 16.7% and 22.1% relative improvements in average NDCG@10 over the strongest visual retrieval baselines and OCR-based text retrieval baselines, respectively. Latent concepts effectively connect local visual cues with semantic relevance and preserve strong retrieval alignment.

Conclusion: Latent concepts provide an effective bridge between visual evidence and semantic queries, enabling nuanced capture of both fine-grained textual cues and complex document-level visual structures, while maintaining strong retrieval performance. Code and data are publicly available.

Abstract: Visual document retrieval is a critical component of multimodal retrieval-augmented generation, aiming to identify query-relevant pages from document collections where evidence is distributed across text, layout, charts, and visual structures. Recent efforts toward finer-grained supervision primarily rely on textual descriptions or localized visual regions as evidence proxies. However, such supervision signals may either overlook complex visual structures or provide incomplete and inaccurate representations of the underlying evidence. To address these limitations, we propose ConceptFormer, a latent concept representation learning framework for visual document retrieval. ConceptFormer models query-relevant evidence as continuous, query-conditioned latent concepts that explicitly bridge localized visual evidence and semantic relevance, without requiring either textual intermediate representations or direct reliance on raw visual annotations. During training, ConceptFormer employs a strong vision-language model to dynamically determine the number of latent concept tokens and uses these concepts as an intermediate representation to bridge the semantic gap between queries and documents, thereby guiding the learning of the embedding space. Experiments on diverse visual document retrieval benchmarks demonstrate that ConceptFormer achieves 16.7\% and 22.1\% relative improvements in average NDCG@10 over the strongest visual retrieval baseline and the strongest OCR-based text retrieval baseline, respectively. Further analysis reveals that latent concepts effectively connect localized visual evidence with semantic relevance, enabling the retriever to capture both fine-grained textual cues and complex document-level visual structures while preserving strong retrieval alignment. Codes and data are available at https://github.com/Neuir/ConceptFormer.

</details>


### [109] [What You Ask is What You Ground: Bridging Question Intent to Temporal Evidence for Grounded VideoQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15708)
*Jinhwan Seo,Kyubeom Han,Jumin Lee,Junhyug Noh,Sung-eui Yoon*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GroundFormer tackles question-invariant grounding in grounded video QA by conditioning video features on question intent, using communication tokens for directed visuo-lingual interaction, a factorized MIL cross-attention for temporal evidence and answer coupling, Gaussian smoothing for coherent segments, and a hierarchical multi-modal contrastive loss in a two-pass pipeline, achieving state-of-the-art results on NExT-GQA and STAR with improved question-discriminative grounding.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Identify and mitigate a failure mode in grounded VideoQA where models predict similar temporal segments for different questions about the same video due to modality isolation and weak question integration.

Method: GroundFormer conditions video features on question intent via learnable communication tokens to enable directed visuo-lingual interaction. A factorized MIL cross-attention operates on question-conditioned features to jointly select answers and temporal evidence under candidate-level supervision, with Gaussian smoothing converting attention peaks into coherent temporal segments. A hierarchical multi-modal contrastive loss aligns video, question, and answer embeddings across a two-pass training pipeline.

Result: Achieves state-of-the-art grounded VideoQA performance on NExT-GQA and STAR datasets, with substantial improvements in question-discriminative temporal grounding.

Conclusion: By addressing modality isolation and weak question injection, GroundFormer introduces question-conditioned video representations, token-mediated cross-modal interaction, and multi-modal contrastive learning to produce more discriminative temporal grounding and superior performance on benchmark datasets.

Abstract: We study a critical yet overlooked failure mode in Grounded Video Question Answering: question-invariant grounding, where models predict nearly identical temporal segments for different questions about the same video. We trace this behavior to two structural limitations in prior common designs: (i) modality isolation that fixes video representations before they receive question semantics, and (ii) weak question injection inside the grounding module. To address this, we propose GroundFormer, which conditions video features on question intent before localization via learnable communication tokens that mediate directed visuo-lingual interaction. On top of the question-conditioned features, a factorized MIL cross-attention couples answer selection with temporal evidence under candidate-level supervision, while Gaussian smoothing converts peaked attention into temporally coherent segments. We further introduce a hierarchical multi-modal contrastive loss that aligns video, question, and answer embeddings across a two-pass training pipeline. GroundFormer achieves state-of-the-art grounded VideoQA performance on NExT-GQA and STAR, substantially improving question-discriminative temporal grounding.

</details>


### [110] [Beyond Single Object: Learning 3D Relations with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15710)
*Kohsuke Ide,Ryousuke Yamada,Yue Qiu,Xianzheng Ma,Yoshihiro Fukuhara,Hirokatsu Kataoka,Yutaka Satoh*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A three-part framework for detailed multi-object reasoning in 3D-LLMs: MO3D dataset, Multi-3DLLM with Patch-Interaction Transformer, and Mini-app benchmarks; achieves state-of-the-art on MO3D and benefits single-object tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current 3D-LLMs and 2D-VLMs lack fine-grained inter-object comparison and geometric awareness across multiple objects; a dedicated dataset, architecture, and benchmarks are needed to enable object-level reasoning in 3D. 

Method: Introduce MO3D as an instruction dataset requiring fine-grained multi-object comparison; develop Multi-3DLLM using a Patch-Interaction Transformer (PIT) to model inter-/intra-object relations while preserving local geometry; design Mini-apps (Shape Mating, Change Captioning) to probe geometric understanding in practical tasks.

Result: Multi-3DLLM trained on the mixture data surpasses all baselines on MO3D and shows positive transfer to single-object classification.

Conclusion: The framework demonstrates that a combination of task-specific data, a geometry-aware inter-object model, and application-driven benchmarks yields improved detail-oriented 3D reasoning and transfer to related tasks.

Abstract: We address a fundamental gap in 3D-LLMs: existing models focus on single-object/scene description, struggling with detailed, inter-object comparison. We propose a framework for detailed object-level reasoning across multiple objects with three components: (1) MO3D (Multi-Object in 3D), an instruction dataset requiring fine-grained multi-object comparison; (2) Multi-3DLLM, using a minimal Patch-Interaction Transformer (PIT) that models inter-/intra-object relationships while preserving local geometry; (3) Mini-apps, two application-driven benchmarks (Shape Mating, Change Captioning) that probe geometric understanding for practical use. Recent 3D-LLMs and 2D-VLMs perform poorly on these tasks, lacking both comparison-centric design and geometric awareness. In contrast, Multi-3DLLM trained on our mixture data learns geometric reasoning, surpasses all baselines on MO3D, and provides positive transfer to single-object classification.

</details>


### [111] [YOLO26-RD: An End-to-End Road Damage Detection Network With Learnable Contrast Enhancement and Edge-Guided Downsampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15713)
*Sompote Youwai,Pawarotorn Chaipetch,Hathairat Samaikul,Theerayut Yonseng*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A data-first audit challenges the small-object premise in automated pavement distress detection and yields a streamlined YOLO26-RD detector with LearnableContrast and EdgeSPD; removing P2 improves speed and mAP, with best results on a 7.6k-image road crack dataset; residual errors traced to distribution shift and label issues; they release the audit protocol.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the common framing of pavement-distress detection as a small-object problem and assess whether high-resolution P2/4 detection is necessary, using a data-driven audit to guide architectural choices.

Method: End-to-end NMS-free detector based on YOLO26 (YOLO26-RD) with two lightweight modules: LearnableContrast (494 params, differentiable CLAHE-like per-tile contrast) and EdgeSPD (Sobel-gated space-to-depth downsampler, +2 params). Dataset of 7,618 images (alligator crack, linear crack, patching). Train from scratch at 640x640. Ablations removing P2 level but keeping P2 features in fusion. Evaluate mAP50; analyze failure modes; release audit protocol.

Result: Removing P2 improves mAP50 by 2.8 points over full YOLO26-RD and reduces epoch time by 8%. Best screening config achieves 0.787 mAP50 on validation, versus 0.771 baseline (stock YOLO26-s). Patchings gain 2.6 points vs baseline; 9.4 over unmodified YOLO26-RD. Residual errors for cracks attributed to distribution shift, sub-pixel width at 640x640, label incompleteness. Audit protocol released.

Conclusion: For pavement imagery, subtractive measurement-based design (pruning levels) outperforms adding modules; a data-first audit can guide architecture and rely less on high-resolution detection heads; dataset-specific issues dominate performance for the rare classes.

Abstract: Automated pavement-distress detection is commonly framed as a small-object problem, motivating high-resolution P2/4 detection heads and lossless downsampling. We present YOLO26-RD, an end-to-end (NMS-free) detector built on YOLO26 with two lightweight novel modules (LearnableContrast, a 494-parameter differentiable analogue of CLAHE that adapts contrast per tile inside the network, and EdgeSPD, a Sobel-gated space-to-depth downsampler adding only 2 parameters over SPD-Conv), and we subject the design to a data-first audit on a 7,618-image road-survey dataset (alligator crack, linear crack, patching). The audit falsifies the small-object premise: 92% of instances are COCO-large, and linear cracks are extreme-aspect structures (median 10:1) whose difficulty is sensitivity, not localization. Guided by this analysis, we remove the P2 detection level while retaining P2 features in the fusion path, which improves mAP50 by 2.8 points over the full YOLO26-RD model and reduces epoch time by 8%. Trained from scratch at 640x640, our best screening configuration reaches 0.787 mAP50 on the validation split versus a 0.771 project baseline (a stock YOLO26-s of uncontrolled recipe), with the largest per-class gain on the rarest class (patching, 2.6 points over baseline; 9.4 over the unmodified YOLO26-RD control under an identical recipe). A failure-mode decomposition further attributes the residual error of the bottleneck class (crack, approximately 0.74 across all architectures tested) to train/validation distribution shift on crack orientation and length, sub-pixel crack width at 640x640, and label incompleteness, factors no architecture change can address. We argue that for pavement imagery, measurement-driven subtraction outperforms module accretion, and we release our audit protocol alongside the model.

</details>


### [112] [Anatomical and Physical Supervision for CT-less PET Attenuation Correction: BIC-MAC 2026 Challenge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15721)
*Petros Chatzitoulousis,George K. Matsopoulos*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Multimodal anatomy- and physics-supervised nnU-Net for CT-less PET attenuation correction via pseudo-CT synthesis, leveraging a frozen segmentation extractor and differentiable projection loss; initialized from MR-to-CT weights; shows improved pseudo-CT quality and PET reconstructions with minimal architectural changes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: CT-less PET attenuation correction is essential for reducing radiation exposure and increasing accessibility. Leveraging anatomical priors and physical attenuation constraints can improve pseudo-CT fidelity and downstream PET accuracy beyond purely data-driven approaches.

Method: nnU-Net-based pipeline with (1) anatomical supervision using a frozen TotalSegmentator feature extractor, anatomy-guided structural constraints, and patch sampling; (2) physical supervision via a differentiable attenuation correction factor projection loss derived from multi-angle attenuation projections; (3) pretrained initialization from SynthRAD MR-to-CT; (4) minimal architectural modifications; (5) preprocessing, plan, and supervision design enhancements across the pipeline.

Result: Reported improvements in pseudo-CT quality and downstream PET reconstruction; demonstrates that integrating anatomical guidance with attenuation physics within an efficient nnU-Net framework yields better CT-less PET attenuation correction.

Conclusion: Combining anatomical supervision with physics-informed attenuation losses, within a scalable nnU-Net pipeline, provides an effective route for CT-less PET attenuation correction via high-quality pseudo-CT synthesis.

Abstract: This report describes our submission to the Big Cross-Modal Attenuation Correction (BIC-MAC) 2026 Challenge for CT-less PET attenuation correction through multimodal pseudo-CT synthesis. We build upon a standard nnU-Net architecture and combine anatomical and physical supervision to improve both pseudo-CT quality and downstream PET reconstruction. Anatomical supervision is introduced through a frozen TotalSegmentator feature extractor, anatomy-guided structural constraints and patch sampling, while physical supervision is achieved using a differentiable attenuation correction factor projection loss based on multi-angle attenuation projections. Furthermore, the network is initialized with pretrained weights obtained from training on the SynthRAD Challenge MR-to-CT dataset. Minimal architectural modifications are applied, while performance improvements are pursued across the nnU-Net pipeline, including preprocessing, plans, and supervision design, among other components. Our final submission demonstrates the effectiveness of combining anatomical supervision, attenuation physics, and efficient nnU-Net scaling for CT-less PET attenuation correction.

</details>


### [113] [ES3D: Embedding Semantics into 3D Space for Component-Aware Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15749)
*Xuancheng Jin,Rengan Xie,Jiayuan Lu,Wenting Zheng,Rui Wang,Yuchi Huo,Lincheng Li,Yingfeng Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ES3D embeds semantics directly into 3D space to enable component-aware retrieval and editing of 3D assets, using multi-view semantic projections for retrieval and an inpainting-guided edit with a pretrained 3D generative model.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing 3D editing methods struggle with fine-grained control and semantic understanding: text-driven edits are coarse, manual 3D masks are required, and non-target regions change undesirably due to lack of fine-grained semantics.

Method: Construct a 3D semantic embedding by projecting multi-view semantic features into the asset's voxelized space. Retrieve editable components by comparing this 3D semantic embedding with embeddings of image/text queries. For edits, use a pretrained 3D generative model with inpainting to modify the retrieved components guided by user-provided images while preserving the rest of the asset.

Result: Demonstrates geometrically consistent and semantically coherent edits, enabling robust image-based and text-assisted control for 3D editing through component-aware retrieval and localized editing.

Conclusion: ES3D offers a semantics-embedded 3D editing framework that retrieves editable regions via semantic cues and conditions from multiple images, improving fine-grained control over 3D edits.

Abstract: Existing 3D editing methods have made notable progress in controllability, yet they remain limited in several important ways. Most approaches rely on text-driven editing, which struggles to express fine-grained visual changes intended by the user. Moreover, many methods require manually supplied 3D masks or introduce unintended changes to regions that should remain untouched. These limitations largely arise from the absence of fine-grained semantic understanding, making it difficult for existing models to retrieve or modify specific 3D components.
  We introduce ES3D, a framework that embeds semantics directly into 3D space, enabling component-aware retrieval and editing of a 3D asset conditioned on multiple local reference images and optional text queries. We first construct a 3D semantic embedding by projecting multi-view semantic features into the voxelized space of the asset. We then perform 3D component retrieval by computing feature similarity between the 3D semantic embedding and the semantic embeddings of image or text queries. For editing, we employ a pretrained 3D generative model with an inpainting mechanism to modify the retrieved components guided by user-provided images while preserving the rest of the asset. Overall, ES3D is a 3D editing framework that retrieves editable regions based on semantic cues and uses multiple images as conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ES3D produces geometrically consistent and semantically coherent edits, enabling robust image-based and text-assisted control for 3D editing.

</details>


### [114] [Beyond Independence: Learning Correlated Views for Variational Incomplete Multi-View Clustering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15757)
*Zheming Xu,Aiyue Tang,Shidi Chen,Xuechao Zou,Congyan Lang,Rogelio A. Mancisidor,Michael Kampffmeyer*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A variational IMVC method with a learnable cross-view correlation modeled via a normalized Cholesky parameterization of the posterior-error covariance; outperforms state-of-the-art across missing views with minimal parameter overhead.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing variational IMVC methods rely on conditional independence across views during aggregation, which fails to capture inherent cross-view correlations in multi-view data.

Method: Model a cross-view covariance of posterior estimation errors; represent the correlation matrix with a normalized Cholesky decomposition to ensure positive definiteness; integrate into a unified variational objective; train end-to-end.

Result: Extensive experiments on multiple IMVC benchmarks show consistent improvement over SOTA across various missing-view settings, with negligible extra parameters.

Conclusion: Adaptive cross-view correlation modeling is effective for IMVC and highlights the need to move beyond independence assumptions; code available at GitHub.

Abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC) aims to uncover shared cluster structures from data with partially observed views. Although recent imputation-free methods based on variational inference demonstrate robustness to missing views, they commonly rely on a conditional independence assumption across views in the posterior aggregation stage, which fails to capture the inherently structured and potentially correlated nature of multi-view data. In this paper, we propose a variational framework that explicitly goes beyond this assumption by introducing a learnable cross-view correlation structure. Specifically, we explicitly model and learn correlations between views by utilizing the covariance structure of posterior estimation errors during aggregation. To facilitate robust and efficient learning, the correlation matrix is parameterized through a normalized Cholesky decomposition, ensuring positive definiteness and enabling the entire model to be trained jointly through a unified variational objective. Extensive experiments on multiple IMVC benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across diverse missing-view settings while introducing only a negligible number of learnable parameters. These results highlight the effectiveness of adaptive correlation modeling in variational IMVC, demonstrating the need to go beyond the independence assumption in IMVC. The code is available at https://github.com/zmxu196/ACOVA.

</details>


### [115] [ChainSpace: A Chained-Reasoning Paradigm for Spatial Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15788)
*Xiaohan Zhang,Feng Gu,Xudong Rao,Xuhao Pan,Tao Wei,Zhou Pan,Kun Zhan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ChainSpace introduces a chained-reasoning paradigm for spatial intelligence, structuring reasoning as a state-preserving, multi-round process. It yields ChainSpace-Bench (manual multi-round real-world benchmark with chain-aware metric) and ChainSpace-Pipeline (simulator-generated chain supervision). Results show chain-level failures are missed by isolated QA, and data-efficient training yields competitive performance and transfer to external benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing data-centric spatial reasoning treats reasoning as isolated QA tasks, enabling shortcut-based answers and providing limited supervision for persistent spatial understanding. There is a need for state-preserving, chain-consistent reasoning to improve fidelity and data efficiency in spatial intelligence.

Method: ChainSpace frameworks: (1) ChainSpace-Bench—a manually annotated real-world multi-round benchmark with a Chain-Aware Metric that enforces chain consistency; (2) ChainSpace-Pipeline—a simulator-based framework to generate chain-structured supervision for training, enabling data-efficient learning. Spatial questions are organized into logically constrained, jointly consistent chains where later questions depend on earlier spatial constraints.

Result: Empirical findings indicate chain-level failures are exposed by ChainSpace-Bench that are not captured by isolated question accuracy. With relatively small amounts of simulator-generated chained data, models trained via ChainSpace-Pipeline achieve the best performance among open-source models on ChainSpace-Bench and transfer competitively to multiple external spatial intelligence benchmarks.

Conclusion: ChainSpace provides a faithful evaluation framework and data-efficient training paradigm for spatial intelligence by enforcing chain-consistent, state-preserving reasoning across multi-round tasks.

Abstract: Spatial intelligence requires foundation models to maintain coherent spatial state across interactions with the physical world. However, existing data-centric approaches typically treat spatial reasoning as independent question-answer instances, enabling shortcut-based answering and providing limited supervision for persistent spatial understanding. To address this, we introduce ChainSpace, a chained-reasoning paradigm that structures spatial reasoning as a state-preserving multi-round process. In this paradigm, spatial questions are organized into logically constrained and jointly consistent chains, where later questions depend on spatial constraints established in earlier rounds. Following this principle, we instantiate ChainSpace-Bench, a manually annotated real-world multi-round benchmark with a Chain-Aware Metric, and ChainSpace-Pipeline, a simulator-based chain-structured supervision generation framework for spatial intelligence training. Experiments show that ChainSpace-Bench exposes chain-level failures that are not captured by isolated question accuracy. Additionally, with a relatively small amount of simulator-generated chained data, models trained by ChainSpace-Pipeline achieve the best performance among open-source models on ChainSpace-Bench and transfer competitively to multiple external spatial intelligence benchmarks. These results establish ChainSpace as an effective paradigm for more faithful evaluation and more data-efficient learning of spatial intelligence.

</details>


### [116] [PWLR: Pairwise Witness Local Rejection for Boundary-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15802)
*Chengyao Jia,Ruixuan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PWLR introduces pairwise language-guided local verifications to augment vision–language OOD detectors. An offline multi-language model generates local cues that discriminate ID classes from specific rivals; these cues are filtered using ID-only data with a frozen backbone. Inference calibrates global class scores with pairwise local evidence, improving near- and far-OOD detection across backbones on ImageNet-100 benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Near-OOD samples near ID boundaries challenge OOD detection. While vision-language models benefit from semantics or prompting, explicit boundary evidence from language is rarely used to separate confusing ID classes. PWLR leverages language to provide boundary cues to distinguish close ID rivals.

Method: 1) Use an offline multilingual LLM to describe local cues that favor an ID class over a rival. 2) Screen these cue phrases with ID-only data under a frozen vision-language backbone to keep reliable local verifiers. 3) At inference, retain a small set of globally plausible classes, assess local support against their most relevant rivals, and fuse this pairwise evidence with calibrated global class scores.

Result: Empirical results show consistent improvements of strong vision-language baselines across multiple backbones on ImageNet-100 far-OOD, cleaner/challenging OOD, and near-OOD benchmarks. Source code will be released.

Conclusion: PWLR provides a boundary-aware, language-guided local verification framework that complements global scores, improving OOD detection in vision-language models with modest additional supervision from offline LLMs and a screening step.

Abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection remains challenging for image classifiers, especially when near-OOD samples lie close to in-distribution (ID) class boundaries. Recent vision-language detectors improve OOD detection through class semantics, local prompting, or LLM-generated outlier concepts, but seldom use language as explicit boundary evidence between confusing ID classes. We propose Pairwise Witness Local Rejection (PWLR), which uses an MLLM offline to describe visible local cues that favor one ID class over a specific rival class. These cue phrases are then screened with ID-only data under a frozen vision-language backbone, so that only reliable local verifiers are kept. At inference, PWLR first retains a small set of globally plausible classes, then checks whether any of them is locally supported against its most relevant rivals, and finally combines this pairwise local evidence with the global class score through calibration. Experiments on ImageNet-100 far-OOD, cleaner/challenging OOD and near-OOD benchmarks show that PWLR consistently improves strong vision-language baselines across multiple backbones. Source code will be released.

</details>


### [117] [From Generation to Matching: A Development Report on Personalized Chinese Handwriting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15812)
*Yiwei Liu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Shift from few-shot synthesis to character-wise matching within a frozen real-ink pipeline, achieving broad candidate coverage and stable B-level handwriting quality, with outputs frequently near A-level under a USER-defined criterion; generation deemed unnecessary for this case.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Assess whether personalized handwriting can be produced via generation or matching, addressing the tension between structural regularization (canonicalization) and preserving user identity in strokes; explore practicality via an equivalence-class and cross-writer assembly.

Method: Start with ~200 real samples from a single user across 197 characters; attempt few-shot generation for unseen characters; observe canonicalization vs personalization conflict; pivot to real-human equivalence classes; leverage a multi-writer CASIA candidate pool to locate user-compatible realizations; switch task from synthesis to character-wise matching and then cross-writer composition into a virtual writer; deploy a frozen system using real-ink features, character-specific population percentiles, top-20 pruning, and greedy hardest-first whole-row selection.

Result: All 197 USER characters had real-human candidates; 100-character evaluation subset achieved 100/100 coverage; a row was visually almost indistinguishable from the USER handwriting; a 60-episode stability audit placed outputs in an A-like machine-proxy region (not independent human A-level judgments); overall evidence supports stable, practical B-level quality with many outputs near A-level under the USER-defined criterion.

Conclusion: Generation became unnecessary for this specific case; does not claim universal or unrestricted handwriting synthesis.

Abstract: This paper documents a frozen engineering project on personalized Chinese handwriting. The project started from approximately 200 real handwriting images from one user, covering 197 unique Chinese characters, and was initially formulated as few-shot generation of unseen characters. A sequence of canonical-centered personalization routes repeatedly exposed the same conflict: increasing structural pressure made outputs more canonical, while increasing personalization could damage identity-defining strokes. The project was therefore reset around real-human character equivalence classes. A multi-writer CASIA candidate pool showed that a USER-compatible realization often already existed among valid human samples. The task consequently changed from synthesis to character-wise matching, followed by cross-writer composition into a virtual writer. The frozen system uses real-ink features, character-specific human population percentiles, top-20 candidate pruning, and greedy hardest-first whole-row selection. On the covered target set, all 197 USER characters had real-human candidates, and the 100-character evaluation subset was covered 100/100. Knowncharacter held-out comparisons included a row judged visually almost indistinguishable from genuine USER handwriting. A 60- episode stability audit placed every episode in a predefined A-like machine-proxy region, but these were not independent human A-level judgments. The final evidence supports stable practical B-level quality, with many outputs approaching A-level under the USER-defined criterion. The report records why generation became unnecessary for this case without claiming unrestricted or universal handwriting synthesis.

</details>


### [118] [FlowDance: Music-Driven Dance Video Generation with Parallel Pose and RGB Streams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15818)
*Genying Li,Boda Lin,Jiachen Li,Zijian Jia,Haojie Zheng,Yiming Wang,Shuchen Weng,Si Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FlowDance is a music-driven dance video synthesis framework that uses parallel pose and RGB streams with timestep-aware pose injection and persistent identity injection to animate a reference person while preserving identity, plus a high-resolution in-the-wild dataset with synchronized music, 3D motion, and pose annotations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The task demands jointly learning music-to-motion correspondence, identity-preserving animation, temporal coherence, and realistic video generation, which is difficult due to the need for coordinated motion structure and consistent appearance across frames.

Method: FlowDance integrates explicit motion modeling with reference-preserving visual synthesis via parallel pose and RGB streams. It introduces timestep-aware pose injection to adapt structural guidance across denoising steps and persistent identity injection to maintain the reference appearance over long video sequences. The work also provides a high-quality dataset with synchronized music, RGB videos, 3D motion, camera parameters, and 2D pose annotations.

Result: Extensive experiments show that FlowDance achieves strong performance in both dance motion generation and music-driven dance video synthesis, demonstrating the effectiveness of the joint motion-visual framework and the proposed injection mechanisms.

Conclusion: FlowDance effectively combines explicit motion control with reference-preserving visual synthesis, enabling realistic and identity-consistent music-driven dance videos; the accompanying dataset supports robust evaluation and future research in music–motion–video synthesis.

Abstract: Music-driven dance video synthesis aims to animate a reference person according to a given music clip. The task is challenging because it requires a model to jointly learn music-to-motion correspondence, identity-preserving human animation, temporal coherence, and visually realistic video generation. We present FlowDance, a music-driven dance video generation framework that integrates explicit motion modeling with reference-preserving visual synthesis through parallel pose and RGB streams. We further introduce timestep-aware pose injection to adapt structural guidance across denoising steps and persistent identity injection to preserve the reference appearance over long video. To support this task, we further build a popularity-curated, high-resolution in-the-wild dance video dataset with synchronized music, RGB videos, 3D body motion, camera parameters, and projected 2D pose annotations. Extensive experiments show that FlowDance achieves strong performance in both dance motion generation and music-driven dance video synthesis.

</details>


### [119] [MITE-Net: SWaP-Optimized 4K Video Tiny Target Perception for Embodied Edge SAR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15830)
*Mingshuo Xu,Mu Hua,Jigen Peng,Qi Wang,Shigang Yue*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A SWaP-optimized 4K tiny target perception framework (MITE-Net) combining a learning-free TT-Motion-based Region Proposal Network with a tiny R-CNN head, a standardized SAR-Tiny dataset suite, and edge-device benchmarks, delivering real-time performance and superior energy efficiency, with urban-scene limitations identified.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-time detection of extremely small targets under strict size, weight, and power constraints on edge devices (e.g., UAVs) is hampered by feature loss from downsampling and latency from slice-based processing; there is a need for standardized 4K tiny-target evaluation for SAR applications.

Method: Develop MITE-Net: a cascaded architecture where a bio-inspired, learning-free Tiny Target Motion-Based RPN provides proposals to a sub-0.14M-parameter R-CNN-like head. Assemble SAR-Tiny by relabeling SeaDroneSee-Tiny and UAVID-Tiny datasets for 4K tiny targets. Benchmark on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier with 4K input, compare to YOLO baselines, report FPS and power consumption.

Result: MITE-Net achieves 100% search success at 30.33 FPS on 4K maritime imagery and consumes 3.19 W (9.51 FPS/W), outperforming YOLO baselines in target recall and energy efficiency. UAVID-Tiny reveals that the learning-free front-end struggles in urban clutter, while the ultra-lightweight head lacks capacity for complex features.

Conclusion: The work delivers an efficient onboard perception paradigm and provides a rigorous SAR-Tiny baseline for end-to-end SAR architectures, including standardized 4K tiny-target evaluation; it also identifies limitations to guide future improvements in urban environments.

Abstract: Real-time tiny target perception in high-resolution imagery is critical for embodied Search-and-Rescue (SAR) missions. However, strict Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) constraints on edge devices like UAVs create a bottleneck: traditional image downsampling causes severe feature loss, while slice-based processing incurs prohibitive latency. To address this gap, this paper introduces a comprehensive framework encompassing a novel architecture, specialized datasets, and hardware-level benchmarks. First, we propose MITE-Net, a SWaP-optimized cascaded architecture, which couples a bio-inspired, learning-free Tiny Target Motion-Based Region Proposal Network (TTM-RPN) with a sub-0.14M-parameter R-CNN-like head. Second, to standardize 4K tiny target evaluation, we construct the SAR-Tiny Datasets by relabeling two challenging UAV datasets: SeaDroneSee-Tiny (dynamic maritime scenes, tiny targets predominantly of 64-256 pixels ) and UAVID-Tiny (cluttered urban scenes, extremely tiny targets, less than 64 pixels). Third, we benchmark against state-of-the-art YOLO models on an edge device, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier, where MITE-Net directly processes 4K maritime imagery, achieving a 100\% search success rate at 30.33 FPS. Consuming merely 3.19 W (9.51 FPS/W), MITE-Net vastly outperforms YOLO baselines in target recall and energy efficiency. Conversely, UAVID-Tiny evaluations expose a compound structural limitation: the learning-free bionic front-end struggles against urban backgrounds, while the ultra-lightweight head lacks representational capacity for complex features. Ultimately, this work delivers an efficient onboard perception paradigm and a rigorous baseline guiding future end-to-end SAR architectures.

</details>


### [120] [CardiacMamba: Fair and Robust RGB-RF Fusion for Remote Heart Rate Estimation via State Space Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15831)
*Bo Zhao,Zheng Wu,Yiping Xie,Zitong YU*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Fair and robust RGB-RF fusion for remote heart-rate estimation (CardiacMamba) using TDMM, bidirectional SSM interaction, and CFFT; achieves state-of-the-art on EquiPleth with strong fairness across skin tones and robustness to RGB/RF degradation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: RGB-only rPPG is sensitive to lighting, motion, and skin-tone bias; need modality fusion to improve robustness and fairness.

Method: CardiacMamba framework integrating optical facial cues and RF cardiac motion cues via state-space modeling; introduces Temporal Difference Mamba Module (TDMM) to enhance RF temporal variations; bidirectional SSM-based interaction to align RGB-RF dynamics; Channel-wise FFT (CFFT) for channel spectral refinement.

Result: On EquiPleth: MAE 0.96 bpm, RMSE 3.06 bpm, Pearson 0.97; reduces light-dark skin-tone MAE gap to 0.26 bpm; robust under RGB degradation and RF-missing conditions; state-of-the-art performance.

Conclusion: CardiacMamba provides fair, robust RGB-RF fusion for rPPG, achieving high accuracy and better fairness across skin tones with robust performance under modality perturbations.

Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables non-contact heart rate (HR) monitoring from facial videos, but RGB-only methods are vulnerable to illumination changes, motion artifacts, and skin-tone-dependent optical reflectance. We propose CardiacMamba, a fair and robust RGB-RF fusion framework that integrates optical facial cues and radio-frequency cardiac motion cues through state space modeling. CardiacMamba introduces a Temporal Difference Mamba Module (TDMM) to enhance subtle RF temporal variations, a bidirectional SSM-based interaction mechanism to align heterogeneous RGB-RF dynamics, and a Channel-wise Fast Fourier Transform (CFFT) module for channel-domain spectral refinement. On the EquiPleth dataset, CardiacMamba achieves state-of-the-art performance with 0.96 bpm MAE, 3.06 bpm RMSE, and 0.97 Pearson correlation, while reducing the observed light-dark skin-tone MAE gap to 0.26 bpm and maintaining robustness under RGB degradation and RF-missing conditions

</details>


### [121] [Beyond Visual CoT: Internalized Visual Thinking for Proactive Video Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15869)
*Xiaoyu Zhu,Xinke Deng,Suresh Taddewadikar,Arnab Kumar Mondal,Zhongyu Jiang,Ian Fasel,Joerg Liebelt*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Internalized Visual Thinking (IVT) is a post-training framework that learns to predict future frame embeddings during training, enabling direct textual answers at inference without synthesizing future frames, achieving competitive accuracy with much lower latency than Visual CoT.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Visual CoT provides intuitive visual chain-of-thought via intermediate image generation but incurs heavy inference overhead, hindering proactive video reasoning. IVT aims to internalize visual reasoning during training so inference can be direct and efficient.

Method: Train on unlabeled videos to jointly optimize textual prediction and next-embedding prediction. Given a partially observed video, IVT predicts latent representations of future frames along with the target answer. At inference, the model outputs the answer without generating or re-encoding future frames. The study conducts extensive ablations over target representations, decoder designs, horizons, data mixtures, curricula, and objectives.

Result: IVT outperforms direct-answer fine-tuning across six evaluation settings while keeping the same inference pathway. Compared to explicit Visual CoT, IVT delivers comparable or better performance and over 5× end-to-end latency reduction. The findings suggest explicit pixel-space generation at inference may be unnecessary for proactive video reasoning; predictive world modeling can be internalized during training to yield more accurate and efficient multimodal reasoners.

Conclusion: Internalizing predictive visual reasoning during training can replace real-time pixel-space generation, enabling efficient and accurate proactive video reasoning without sacrificing performance.

Abstract: Multimodal large language models increasingly use visual chain-of-thought (Visual CoT) to reason about spatial, temporal, and embodied environments. By generating intermediate reasoning images, Visual CoT provides an intuitive mechanism for visual foresight but introduces substantial inference overhead, which is particularly problematic for proactive video reasoning. We ask whether models can learn to think visually during training while reasoning directly at inference. We introduce Internalized Visual Thinking (IVT), a post-training framework that jointly optimizes textual prediction and next-embedding prediction over unlabeled videos. Given a partially observed video, IVT predicts latent representations of future frames together with the target textual answer, encouraging the model to capture motion, object transitions, interactions, and latent intent. At inference, IVT generates the answer directly without synthesizing or re-encoding future frames. We conduct controlled studies across target representations, decoder designs, prediction horizons, data mixtures, training curricula, and predictive objectives. IVT improves over direct-answer fine-tuning on all six evaluation settings while retaining the same inference pathway. Compared with explicit Visual CoT, IVT achieves comparable or better performance and reduces average end-to-end latency by more than 5x. Together, our findings suggest that explicit pixel-space generation at inference time, as used in visual chain-of-thought, may not be necessary for effective proactive video reasoning. Predictive world modeling can be internalized during training to produce multimodal reasoners that are both more accurate and substantially more efficient.

</details>


### [122] [CLARA: Clip-Level Multimodal Alignment with VLM-Derived Rationales for Hateful Video Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15905)
*Yuchen Zhang,Shuang Dai,Zeyu Fu,Yunfei Long,Ravi Shekhar,Haralambos Mouratidis*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A clip-level multimodal framework (CLARA) for hateful video detection that models videos as sequences of fine-grained clips to capture temporally localized hateful signals, using a Mixture-of-Experts clip encoder for adaptive multimodal alignment, a local-global segment contrastive objective, and VLM-derived rationales via a gated Transformer; achieves state-of-the-art results on three datasets with comprehensive ablations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Hateful video detection is difficult due to brief, implicit, and temporally dependent multimodal cues (speech, audio, visuals). Treating videos as a single instance loses localized signals; there is a need for fine-grained, temporally aware modeling to improve detection accuracy and robustness.

Method: Proposes CLARA, a clip-level multimodal framework. Key components include a Mixture-of-Experts clip encoder for adaptive alignment across modalities, a local-global segment contrastive objective to capture both short-term cues and long-range dependencies, and integration of VLM-derived rationales through a gated Transformer to provide high-level semantic guidance.

Result: Empirical evaluation on three hateful video datasets shows CLARA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies and parameter analyses validate the contribution and effectiveness of each component.

Conclusion: Modeling videos as sequences of fine-grained clips with adaptive multimodal alignment, contrastive learning at multiple temporal scales, and guidance from high-level semantic rationales yields robust and superior hateful video detection across diverse datasets.

Abstract: Hateful video detection has become increasingly important with the rapid growth of video-centric social media platforms, given the serious risks that hate speech poses to both individual well-being and social cohesion. Compared with text or static multimodal content, hateful video detection remains underexplored and significantly more challenging, as hateful meaning often arises from complex interactions among multimodal cues, including speech, audio, and visual content. Moreover, such signals are often brief, implicit, and temporally dependent, making them difficult to capture using conventional video-level representations. In this work, we propose CLARA, a clip-level multimodal framework for hateful video detection. Instead of treating a video as a single instance, CLARA models it as a sequence of fine-grained clips, enabling more precise capture of temporally localized hateful signals. We introduce a Mixture-of-Experts clip encoder for adaptive multimodal alignment, a local-global segment contrastive objective to jointly model short-term cues and long-range temporal dependencies, and VLM-derived rationales integrated via a gated Transformer to provide high-level semantic guidance. Extensive experiments on three hateful video datasets demonstrate that CLARA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Further ablation studies and parameter analyses validate the effectiveness of each component.

</details>


### [123] [Comprehensive Benchmarking of Deep Learning Architectures for Lung Cancer Histopathology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15915)
*Hadi Hasan,Safaa Salman,Lama Sleem,Ralph Mouawad,Ali Chehab*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A two-stage deep learning framework for lung histopathology: tissue-level classification and pixel-level region segmentation, with comprehensive benchmarking of architectures and end-to-end integration.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address inter-observer variability and manual workload in histopathology by delivering a unified, efficient framework that benchmarks state-of-the-art models for both tasks.

Method: Stage 1: tissue classification using six models (custom CNN, VGG16, DenseNet, MobileNetV3, custom Vision Transformer, YOLO11) on 39k images from LC25000 and LungHist700; Stage 2: segmentation using U-Net, ResNet-encoder U-Net, DeepLabV3+, YOLO11-seg on the GlaS gland segmentation dataset; end-to-end integration of best classifier and segmenter.

Result: Classification: YOLO11 achieves 98.38% accuracy; 5-fold CV 98.21±0.35%; macro F1 0.98. Segmentation: DeepLabV3+ IoU 0.80, Dice 0.89; YOLO11-seg IoU 0.79 with ~14× fewer parameters. End-to-end framework provides accurate, efficient baseline for histopathological analysis.

Conclusion: Demonstrates a competitive, efficient, and reproducible baseline for automated histopathological image analysis by unifying tissue classification and region segmentation within a single framework.

Abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, while histopathological diagnosis is often affected by inter-observer variability and the substantial workload associated with manual slide examination.
