The anchors georeference both a lightweight LiDAR-odometry trajectory and a dense RTAB-Map reconstruction, allowing their outputs to be expressed in a common LUREF frame (geodetic coordinate reference system used in Luxembourg) without requiring GNSS measurements during operation. The method combines coarse similarity alignment with marker-constrained pose-graph optimization. We evaluate it using two handheld acquisition sessions with ground-level and elevated motion profiles emulating UGV and UAV operation. A single iMarker was relocated among six surveyed positions, with the first position revisited to quantify drift correction. Marker-anchor correction reduced revisit inconsistency by 97.9% and 99.1% for the UAV- and UGV-emulating sessions, respectively, and improved held-out anchor prediction compared with one-time alignment. Separately georeferenced dense reconstructions achieved a median cross-session nearest-neighbour distance of 58 cm without explicit cross-session registration. Marker processing operated in real time, while trajectory correction required less than 0.25 s per session. These results demonstrate a proof of concept for georeferencing lightweight odometry and dense reconstructions using visually unobtrusive, pre-surveyed anchors during GNSS-denied operation.

</details>


### [247] [Readiness Barrier Functions: Forward-Invariant Control Authority for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16335)
*Giuseppe Silano*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A forward-invariant actuator-authority control barrier framework for overactuated multirotors reconciles greedy readiness with continuous effort minimization, yielding a compact certified operating set enforced by a torque-level QP and a closed-form readiness bound; it shows robustness to motor-parameter uncertainty and tight performance on hexarotor/octorotor, outperforming greedy strategies in low-authority regimes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To resolve the trade-off between maximizing a readiness metric (which can demand unattainable actuator rates) and maintaining continuous, bounded-wrench performance (which may fail to guarantee a minimum authority). The goal is to certify a guaranteed wrench-rate floor while keeping tracking costs low.

Method: Model authority as a forward-invariant quantity via a control barrier function on the log-determinant of a drag-aware actuator-authority co-metric. Enforce at the torque level with a quadratic program in the allocation null space. Derive a single design inequality that makes the certified set compact and interior to actuator bounds; provide a closed-form readiness cost ln(n/(n−m)) for symmetric designs; formulate a robust variant with a floor shift to handle motor-parameter uncertainty. Analyze tracking via an alignment ratio and provide an O(ρ^{-1/2}) bound on wrench error.

Result: For hexarotor and octorotor platforms, the closed-form-gap matches simulation to machine precision. In authority-scarce regimes, greedy maximization violates the certified floor and incurs wrench errors up to 80× larger than the proposed filter, which maintains invariant certified sets with negligible tracking cost. The robust variant yields a floor shift independent of the airframe matrix, and the performance gap closes under uncertainty.

Conclusion: The framework successfully reconciles readiness maximization with robust authority guarantees, providing explicit, closed-form performance bounds, a compact certified set interior to actuator limits, and superior practical performance over greedy approaches in low-authority scenarios.

Abstract: Allocation schemes that greedily maximize a readiness metric over the actuator fiber bundle of an overactuated multirotor produce commands that jump between disconnected optimal strata, demanding actuator rates no motor can deliver; effort-minimizing schemes are continuous but cannot guarantee that wrench-rate authority stays above any certified level. We reconcile the two by treating authority as a forward-invariant quantity: a control barrier function on the log-determinant of the drag-aware actuator-authority co-metric, enforced at torque level by a quadratic program in the allocation null space. A single design inequality renders the certified set compact and strictly interior to the actuator box, with the readiness cost of any rotor deactivation given in closed form as $\ln(n/(n{-}m))$ for symmetric designs. Tracking is sacrificed only through an explicit alignment ratio, with wrench error bounded by $\mathcal{O}(ρ^{-1/2})$ and a robust variant handles motor-parameter uncertainty with a closed-form floor shift independent of the airframe matrix. On a hexarotor and a fully-actuated octorotor the closed-form gap matches simulation to machine precision; in the authority-scarce regime greedy maximization violates the certified floor and commits wrench errors up to eighty times larger than the proposed filter, which holds invariance of the certified set at negligible tracking cost.

</details>


### [248] [Arm-Aware Guided Dexterous Grasp Generation with Arm-Agnostic Grasp Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16351)
*Yongyi Jia,Yongpeng Jiang,Kangchen Lv,Yi Ren,Mingrui Yu,Xiang Li*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: An inference-time arm-aware dexterous grasp framework that augments pretrained arm-agnostic grasp models with joint hand–arm optimization, guided by closed-form arm constraints, enabling feasible grasps under tight space without retraining.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Hand-centric grasp models alone cannot guarantee collision-free, workspace-constrained grasps; existing arm-aware methods are sample-inefficient or require retraining, limiting generalization across robots/environments.

Method: Formulate joint optimization of hand pose and arm configuration with closed-form gradients for arm constraints; treat hand pose as a diffusion model and show gradient-based optimization is equivalent to guided diffusion sampling to steer toward feasible regions during inference, using arm/environment data only at inference time.

Result: Extensive evaluation on 10k objects across 6 scenarios shows a significantly higher probability of generating feasible grasps in highly constrained settings compared to baseline methods; supplementary materials provided.

Conclusion: The approach enables arm-aware dexterous grasp generation at inference time by leveraging pretrained arm-agnostic models and explicit arm/environment constraints, improving feasibility and generalization in constrained real-world scenarios.

Abstract: Dexterous grasp generation that considers arm-related constraints is crucial in real-world scenarios involving arm environment collision avoidance, workspace boundary grasps, and consecutive grasping. Existing hand-centric grasp models, which primarily focus on the floating hand's pose, are insufficient for such cases. Conventional arm-aware methods either rely on rejection sampling to discard infeasible samples or require retraining on arm-specific data, leading to low sample efficiency under adverse conditions or limited generalization across different robots and environments. To overcome these limitations, this letter presents an arm-aware dexterous grasp generation framework that leverages pretrained arm-agnostic grasp models while integrating arm and environmental information only at inference time. Specifically, we formulate arm-aware constrained grasp generation as a joint optimization of hand pose and arm configuration, and derive closed-form gradients for arm-related constraints. Assuming the hand pose distribution is represented by a diffusion model, we prove that gradient-based optimization is equivalent to guided diffusion sampling, steering near-feasible samples toward the feasible region. Through comprehensive evaluation involving 10k objects across 6 scenarios, we demonstrate that the proposed framework generates feasible grasps in highly constrained settings with significantly higher probability, highlighting its advantages in real-world applications. Supplementary materials and appendix are available at https://arm-aware-dexgrasp.github.io/.

</details>


### [249] [Robot-Body-Aware Traversal Risk Graph Planning for Wheeled-Legged Robots in Complex Terrain](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16433)
*Zhiqiao Guo,Bichi Zhang,Sören Schwertfeger*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Robot-Body-Aware TRG (RB-TRG) extends Traversal Risk Graphs by incorporating heading- and body-footprint-aware risk assessments, enabling more accurate planning for wheeled-legged robots during turns; evaluated on four terrains and MuJoCo with improved success but slightly longer paths; open-source release.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Mitigate limitations of native TRGs that rely on circular neighborhoods and edge-aligned terrain, which can miss partial support loss and body-terrain interference during turning, leading to unsafe or inefficient traversal.

Method: Extend TRG by sampling an oriented rectangular footprint along graph edges with yaw sweeps to quantify longitudinal support variation, lateral inclination, terrain interference, and exposure to untrusted map regions. Use mean and upper-tail features as transition costs and solve with A* over ordered node-pair states, preserving TRG construction and interface.

Result: RB-TRG reduces core geometric body-placement metrics and increases end-to-end success from 51.5% to 68.5%, with mean path length increasing by 2.3%. A Go2-W deployment with full LiDAR navigation stack achieved Best Autonomy and Best Mobility at the IEEE ICRA 2026 Legged Robot Challenges; code released at the provided repository.

Conclusion: RB-TRG provides a body-aware extension to TRG planning that improves traversal reliability for wheeled-legged robots, with a modest increase in path length and demonstrated real-world applicability.

Abstract: Traversal Risk Graphs (TRGs) provide a compact, terrain-aware representation for global navigation, but native TRG costs are computed over circular node neighborhoods and edge-aligned terrain regions rather than the robot's oriented body footprint. For wheeled-legged robots, this abstraction can miss partial support loss and body-terrain interference, especially during turns. We present Robot-Body-Aware TRG planning (RB-TRG), which builds on the sparse TRG representation and lifts edge-wise terrain-risk search to heading- and turn-aware body-risk transitions. An oriented rectangular footprint is sampled along graph edges and yaw sweeps to measure longitudinal support variation, lateral inclination, terrain interference, and exposure to untrusted map regions. Mean-and-upper-tail features are incorporated into transition costs, whose accumulated value is minimized by A* over ordered node-pair states, preserving TRG construction and its planning interface. We evaluate RB-TRG in a same-graph study on four scanned terrain environments and in paired closed-loop MuJoCo trials. RB-TRG reduces the three core geometric body-placement metrics and increases end-to-end success from 51.5% to 68.5%, while increasing mean path length by 2.3%. A Go2-W deployment further demonstrates RB-TRG with a full LiDAR navigation stack, which received the Best Autonomy and Best Mobility awards at the IEEE ICRA 2026 Legged Robot Challenges. The code for RB-TRG is released at https://github.com/ZhiqiaoGuo/RB-TRG.

</details>


### [250] [Observation-Constrained Joint-Space Viewpoint Optimization for Robotic Inspection of Cylindrical Cavities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16442)
*Yuezhong Wang,Rongshen Yin,Bichi Zhang,Sören Schwertfeger*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Autonomous observation-constrained inspection of cylindrical cavities in joint space, optimizing over a set of valid viewing geometries using perception-driven constraints and a multistart derivative-free planner, with collision-aware validation; demonstrated in simulation (Isaac Sim) and hardware.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To satisfy visibility, kinematic, and collision constraints when observing the bottom of cylindrical cavities (as in ASTM search-task benchmarks) without discarding reachable viewpoints.

Method: Represent the objective as a set of valid viewing geometries. Use RGB perception to estimate opening center and cavity axis via arc-supported ellipse fitting with body/side cues. Parameterize constraints on camera-axis alignment, lateral offset, and axial standoff. Apply a multistart derivative-free search in robot joint space with lexicographic priority on constraint satisfaction; rank feasible configurations by motion economy, joint-limit margin, and view quality. Evaluate candidates with a collision-aware motion planner and verify executed pose geometrically and via ray-based bottom visibility.

Result: In Isaac Sim, 92 of 100 target configurations were completed with a mean bottom visibility of 91.65% (vs 76/100 and 84.3% for a multistart coordinate-search baseline). Hardware experiments (tabletop and Unitree A2) demonstrate the complete perception–planning–execution pipeline.

Conclusion: The approach enables autonomous, observation-constrained cavity inspection by combining perception-driven geometry estimation, constraint-based joint-space optimization, and collision-aware planning, yielding higher success rates and better visibility than a baseline in simulation and demonstrated in hardware.

Abstract: Inspection is a core capability in many mobile robotics applications, including industrial facility monitoring, infrastructure maintenance, agriculture, and search and rescue. Observing the bottom of a cylindrical cavity, as required by ASTM search-task benchmarks for response robots, presents a representative challenge: the robot must position its camera precisely while satisfying visibility, kinematic, and collision constraints. This paper presents a fully autonomous method for observation-constrained inspection of cylindrical cavities in robot joint space. Rather than prescribing a single Cartesian camera pose, the method represents the inspection objective as a set of valid viewing geometries, thereby avoiding the rejection of reachable viewpoints and configurations with poor joint-limit margins. An RGB perception front end estimates the opening center and directed cavity axis from semantic masks using arc-supported ellipse fitting together with body and side-generator cues. These estimates parameterize constraints on camera-axis alignment, lateral offset, and axial standoff. A multistart derivative-free search then optimizes robot joint configurations with lexicographic priority given to constraint satisfaction; feasible configurations are ranked according to motion economy, joint-limit margin, and view quality. The resulting candidates are evaluated by a collision-aware motion planner, and the executed camera pose is verified geometrically and using a ray-based estimate of bottom visibility. In Isaac Sim, the proposed method successfully completes 92 of 100 target configurations and attains 91.65% mean bottom visibility among executed trials, compared with 76 of 100 and 84.3% for a multistart coordinate-search baseline. Tabletop and Unitree A2-mounted experiments demonstrate the complete perception-planning-execution pipeline.

</details>


### [251] [Exposing the Long-tail in Embodied Urban Navigation via Scalable Learning from In-the-Wild Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16476)
*Bingyi Xia,Han Bao,Zhewei Chen,Hanjing Ye,Jingwen Yu,Yuhan Pang,Wenjun Xu,Jiankun Wang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A scalable framework learns point-goal urban navigation from uncurated web videos by automatically annotating metric trajectories and semantics, training a vision-language-action policy, and analyzing long-tail performance and failure modes, enabling transfer to real-world navigation tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Data collection for embodied urban navigation is costly and safety-critical scenarios are underrepresented; leveraging web-scale in-the-wild videos can broaden coverage and enable scalable learning.

Method: Automatically annotate uncurated web videos with metric trajectories and structured navigation semantics; train a vision-language-action policy for interpretable navigation planning; characterize the long tail via model performance and perception–motion pattern distributions; apply reflection-based analysis to diagnose recurring failure modes.

Result: Experiments on web-video data and real-world urban navigation tasks show effective knowledge transfer from unconstrained videos and reveal coherent long-tail structures beyond aggregate navigation performance.

Conclusion: The approach provides a scalable pathway to learn embodied urban navigation from unconstrained data, with explicit long-tail analysis and diagnostic tools to improve robustness and transfer to real-world tasks.

Abstract: Learning embodied urban navigation policies from real-world data is constrained by the cost of task-specific data collection and the limited coverage of rare yet safety-critical scenarios. To address these challenges, we present a scalable framework for learning point-goal urban navigation from web-scale in-the-wild egocentric videos while systematically exposing its long tail. The framework automatically annotates uncurated web videos with metric trajectories and structured navigation semantics, which are then used to train a vision-language-action policy for interpretable navigation planning. We characterize the long tail based on model performance and the distribution of perception-motion patterns, and employ reflection-based analysis to diagnose recurring failure modes. Experiments on web-video data and real-world urban navigation tasks demonstrate effective knowledge transfer from unconstrained videos and reveal coherent long-tail structures beyond aggregate navigation performance.

</details>


### [252] [OccamView: Object-Conditioned View Selection for Frame-Budgeted Active 3D Gaussian Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16499)
*Hongbo Gao,Wei Zhang,Zeyu Ni,Dihao Zhu,Ruifeng Li,Yunke Wang,Chang Xu*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: OccamView is an object-conditioned extension to frame-budgeted active 3D Gaussian reconstruction that uses online object memory and occlusion-aware proxies to guide next-best-view selection, augmented by a Geo-Floor constraint; it improves completion metrics on Replica and Matterport3D, especially under tight budgets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Geometry-driven view planning often prioritizes global scene coverage under tight budgets, neglecting partially observed objects. Incorporating object-level cues can steer views to unresolved regions without sacrificing geometry-driven exploration.

Method: Maintain an online memory of detections from open-vocabulary RGB-D observations. Represent uncertain local occupancy around detected objects with conservative hidden-region proxies. Evaluate candidate viewpoints via an occlusion-aware proxy-coverage score. Introduce Geo-Floor to constrain object-conditioned re-ranking to geometrically competitive candidates, preserving the base planner’s exploration behavior.

Result: Experiments on Replica and Matterport3D under a unified frame-budgeted protocol show OccamView consistently improves Completion and Completion Ratio across five budgets, with larger gains at lower frame budgets.

Conclusion: Lightweight object-conditioned cues effectively complement geometry-driven active view planning for frame-budgeted 3D Gaussian reconstruction, enabling better reconstruction of objects without discarding geometry-driven exploration.

Abstract: Active 3D Gaussian reconstruction fundamentally relies on selecting informative next-best views under limited sensing budgets. Existing active 3DGS methods primarily plan viewpoints according to geometric information gain, treating object-induced hidden regions in the same manner as general unexplored space. Under tight frame budgets, such geometry-driven strategies may prioritize global scene coverage while leaving partially observed objects incompletely reconstructed. To address this limitation, we propose OccamView, an object-conditioned view-selection framework for frame-budgeted active 3D Gaussian reconstruction. Rather than predicting unseen object geometry or performing shape completion, OccamView maintains an online object memory from open-vocabulary detections grounded in measured RGB-D observations and represents unresolved local occupancy around detected objects as conservative hidden-region proxies. Candidate viewpoints are then evaluated using an occlusion-aware proxy-coverage score. Furthermore, we introduce a Geo-Floor mechanism that restricts object-conditioned re-ranking to geometrically competitive candidates, allowing object-conditioned cues to guide complementary observations while preserving the geometry-driven exploration behavior of the underlying planner. Experiments on Replica and Matterport3D under a unified frame-budgeted protocol show that OccamView consistently reduces Completion and improves Completion Ratio across five frame budgets, with particularly pronounced gains under limited frame budgets. These results demonstrate that lightweight object-conditioned cues effectively complement geometry-driven active view planning.

</details>


### [253] [NebulaVLA: A Dual-Frequency Vision-Language-Action Model With Guide Action for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16503)
*Cong Zhao,Shuai Tian,Xu Zhang,Baocheng Ni,Xinguo Song,Xueying Sun,Shu Jiang,Shouchang Yang,Bo Tang,Jin Deng,Ge Zhu,YongCheng Wang,Jin Xu,Ri Yang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: NebulaVLA introduces an asynchronous dual-frequency architecture to separate semantic reasoning from low-level action control, paired with GESTURE-7, a unified language-grounded action representation, and the Guide Action algorithm for smooth, continuous motion. It yields state-of-the-art-like efficiency with 85.5% average success on LIBERO-Plus and ~2.7x faster action generation compared to synchronous baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-world VLA systems suffer from efficiency-performance trade-offs, weak cross-embodiment generalization, and choppy execution. A modular, asynchronous design with a unified language-grounded action representation aims to improve efficiency, generalization across heterogeneous robots, and motion smoothness.

Method: An asynchronous dual-frequency architecture decouples high-level semantic reasoning from low-level action control. Introduces GESTURE-7 as a unified language-grounded action representation to bridge semantic gaps across heterogeneous robots. Proposes Guide Action algorithm with mask-based smoothness constraints to enforce kinematic continuity.

Result: NebulaVLA significantly outperforms synchronous baselines, achieving 85.5% average success on LIBERO-Plus and accelerating action generation by ~2.7x, demonstrating improved efficiency and responsiveness in real-world robotics.

Conclusion: Asynchronous design enhances efficiency and responsiveness of VLA systems, enabling better real-world deployment and cross-robot generalization through a unified action representation and smoothness-guided control.

Abstract: Real-world deployment of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models is often bottlenecked by efficiency-performance trade-offs, cross-embodiment generalization, and execution smoothness. We present NebulaVLA, an asynchronous dual-frequency architecture that decouples high-level semantic reasoning from low-level action control, optimizing computational resources and modularity. To bridge semantic gaps across heterogeneous robots, we introduce GESTURE-7, a unified language-grounded action representation. Furthermore, our Guide Action algorithm enforces kinematic continuity via mask-based smoothness constraints. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that NebulaVLA significantly outperforms synchronous baselines, achieving an 85.5\% average success rate on LIBERO-Plus and accelerating action generation by \textasciitilde 2.7$\times$. This asynchronous design enables highly efficient and responsive control for practical robotics.

</details>


### [254] [Co-design of Neural and Muscle Network based on Embodied Perceptron Representation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16555)
*Siyuan Tao,Yoichi Masuda,Hiroyuki Nabae,Masato Ishikawa*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Embodied Perceptron unifies neural networks with physical bodies to enable joint optimization of body and controller; demonstrated on a musculoskeletal robot, yielding inherent stability, better learning efficiency, and smaller models—even with a minimal controller.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is no systematic framework for designing bodies and jointly optimizing them with controllers; reliance on expert intuition limits exploitation of body–environment interactions; a unified theory could enable principled embodied AI design.

Method: Represent physical bodies as perceptrons by mapping mechanical parameters to weights and physical nonlinearities to activation functions; encode physical constraints and nonlinearities into a neural-network-like form; co-optimize the controller and body configuration (e.g., muscle configuration) using this framework.

Result: The framework explains how a body can partially substitute neural control; empirical results show inherent stability, improved learning efficiency, and drastically reduced model size, even with a single-neuron controller.

Conclusion: The Embodied Perceptron provides a theoretical bridge between information and physical dynamics, offering a pathway for systematic design and co-design of embodied AI systems across body–controller interactions.

Abstract: Recent advances in AI technologies have enabled the advanced design of complex control policies. In contrast, focusing on the body, many robots still employ simple bodies that can limit adaptability to environments. Studies in embodied robotics have shown that well-designed bodies can partially replace the role of control and computation with physical body-environment interactions, yet such designs still depend heavily on expert intuition. There is a need for a systematic theoretical framework for body design, as well as a method for joint optimization of the body and controller. To address this, we introduce the Embodied Perceptron, a theoretical framework that unifies neural networks and physical body systems. In this view, the body itself acts as a perceptron: mechanical parameters correspond to weights, and physical nonlinearities play the role of activation functions. By representing physical constraints as weights and nonlinear properties as activation functions, a physical body can be modeled in neural-network form. The system representation enables us to explicitly and theoretically explain that the body can substitute for part of the neural control. As an application, we co-optimize control policy and muscle configuration in a musculoskeletal robot and show that the resulting embodied intelligence can provide inherent stability, improve learning efficiency, and drastically reduce model size-even with a single-neuron controller. The results bridge the informational and physical worlds and provide a pathway toward understanding and systematic design of embodied AI systems.

</details>


### [255] [ViHaTeleop: A Low-Cost, Lightweight Visual-Haptic Teleoperation System for Dexterous Manipulation Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16572)
*Fucai Zhu,Yanhou Lai,Paul Maestre,Koichi Hashimoto*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A lightweight, low-cost visual-haptic teleoperation system (ViHaTeleop) with SLAM-based wrist tracking, camera hand tracking, and finger-wise vibrotactile feedback improves performance on contact-critical tasks and enables a tactile-sim-to-real training pipeline; initial results show increased success rates and perceived contact clarity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Collecting high-quality contact-critical demonstrations with low-cost teleoperation is difficult; incorporating tactile feedback and a tactile proxy in simulation can improve data quality, task performance, and policy learning.

Method: ViHaTeleop system (0.7 kg, $550) featuring SLAM-based wrist tracking, camera-based hand tracking, and LRAs for finger-wide vibrotactile feedback; design choices include LED illumination, fisheye hand camera, and tactile-aware retargeting constraints; deployed on Franka + LEAP Hand + 9DTact in real and simulated environments; evaluation with nine participants across six contact-critical tasks; added depth-camera-based tactile proxy in Isaac Sim to enable a full pipeline from demonstrations to visual-tactile policy training.

Result: Haptics improved success rates across all tasks by +2.2 to +15.6 percentage points; completion-time effects were task-dependent; subjective ratings showed significant increases in contact clarity and grasp confidence (p<0.05). In simulation, tactile cues improved peg-in-hole performance by +17 percentage points over vision-only; preliminary downstream validation indicates tactile cues benefit contact-critical subtasks in learned policies.

Conclusion: ViHaTeleop demonstrates that affordable, tactile-enabled teleoperation improves dexterous manipulation in both real and simulated settings and enables a complete demonstration-to-policy pipeline; results support the value of tactile feedback for contact-critical manipulation tasks.

Abstract: Learning from demonstration is a promising approach for dexterous manipulation, but collecting high-quality contact-critical demonstrations remains difficult with low-cost teleoperation hardware. We present ViHaTeleop, a lightweight (0.7 kg), low-cost (\$550) visual-haptic teleoperation system with SLAM-based wrist tracking, camera-based hand tracking, and finger-wise vibrotactile feedback through Linear Resonant Actuators (LRA). The system includes several design choices (LED illumination, fisheye hand camera, and tactile-aware retargeting constraints) and is deployed on Franka + LEAP Hand + 9DTact in both real and simulated environments. Under matched with/without-haptic conditions with nine participants across six contact-critical tasks, haptics improved success rates across all tasks (+2.2 to +15.6 percentage points), while completion-time effects were task-dependent. Subjective ratings showed significant gains in contact clarity and grasp confidence in both simulation and real-world settings (Wilcoxon signed-rank, $p<0.05$). We also integrate a lightweight depth-camera-based tactile proxy in Isaac Sim, enabling a full pipeline from multi-modal demonstration collection to visual-tactile policy training. Preliminary downstream validation by training visual-tactile policies from collected demonstrations shows tactile cues benefit contact-critical subtasks (peg-in-hole: +17 percentage points over vision-only).

</details>


### [256] [Zetta $ζ$: An Efficient Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16590)
*Xin Ding,Liang Mi,Mingzhe Huang,Zixuan Wang,Chao Zhang,Zixu Hao,Fu Chen,Xiangyu Li,Yikai Zheng,Yaoyu Guo,Weijun Wang,Kun Li,Hao Wu,Yunxin Liu,Ting Cao*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Zetta is a closed-loop embodied learning harness where a frozen base policy is augmented by online-evolved code-based runtime critics and recovery skills, guided by three time-scale loops and Z-Infra for rollout, achieving strong results on robotics benchmarks with big speedups.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome open-loop limitations of end-to-end policies in physical robotics by enabling real-time governance and adaptive skill recovery during execution.

Method: Three time-scale loops: (i) action-frequency governance, (ii) rollout-level critic-recovery proposal, (iii) validation-gated skill updates. Runtime critics and recovery skills evolve online while the base policy remains frozen; Z-Infra decouples agent logic from heterogeneous execution resources to allow scalable rollouts.

Result: State-of-the-art performance on LIBERO-Pro and RoboCasa under the rollout budget: 90.8% and 93.6% success, respectively, with an 11.1× inference speedup; performance scales with self-exploration; zero-shot skill transfer; presence of emergent “Aha Moments.”

Conclusion: Closed-loop harness self-evolution provides a scalable path toward reliable physical intelligence by integrating online policy supervision with frozen core policies.

Abstract: Embodied agents are increasingly used to close the gap left by end-to-end policy models. Yet the agentic path has not realized closed-loop learning in physical execution: existing harnesses remain largely open-loop, following fixed skills during rollout and reflecting only after an episode completes. Such post-hoc reflection cannot govern execution as it unfolds, because physical interaction requires decisions to track rapidly changing robot-environment states at a frequency beyond today's large agentic models. We present Zetta, a closed-loop embodied harness that evolves code-based runtime critics and recovery skills online while keeping the base policy frozen. Through three timescale-separated loops, Zetta provides action-frequency governance, rollout-level critic-recovery proposal, and validation-gated skill updates. Together with Z-Infra, a rollout infrastructure decoupling agent logic from heterogeneous execution resources, Zetta achieves state-of-the-art success on LIBERO-Pro and RoboCasa under our current rollout budget, reaching 90.8% and 93.6%, with an 11.1x inference speedup; success continues to scale with self-exploration experience; learned skills transfer zero-shot, and clear robotic "Aha Moments" emerge. These results show that closed-loop harness self-evolution opens a scaling path for reliable physical intelligence.

</details>


### [257] [DPNet: Efficient Dead-End Prediction and Avoidance for Vision-Based UAV Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16640)
*Ruibin Zhang,Lun Pan,Zelong Xia,Jialiang Hou,Fei Gao*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Lightweight RGB-D neural network predicts relative distance and bearing to potential dead ends within the current field of view to prune a compact trajectory library, enabling fast, proactive dead-end avoidance for vision-based UAVs at 50 Hz onboard; shows zero/manual-annotation transfer to real-world and strong simulation/real-world results.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Vision-based UAVs struggle with dead-end navigation due to limited sensing range and accuracy; there is a need for fast, generalizable dead-end prediction and avoidance that can operate onboard without extensive labeled data.

Method: A lightweight neural network processes RGB-D input from the current field of view to predict the relative distance and bearing to imminent dead ends. These predictions prune a predefined, compact trajectory library, guiding the planner to avoid dead ends. The system runs onboard at 50 Hz, enabling high-frequency replanning and transfer to real-world data without manual annotation or fine-tuning.

Result: In simulation, the approach improves success rate, flight time, and trajectory length, and real-world experiments validate effectiveness in complex scenarios; the method transfers across real-world settings without annotated data or fine-tuning.

Conclusion: Prediction-guided trajectory pruning enables proactive, high-frequency dead-end avoidance in vision-based UAV navigation, with strong generalization to real-world environments and efficient onboard operation.

Abstract: Vision-based Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) often suffer from navigation failures in dead ends due to limited sensing accuracy and range. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a systematic solution for efficient dead-end prediction and avoidance. The proposed method introduces a lightweight neural network to predict the relative distance and bearing of potential dead ends within the current field of view using RGB-D inputs. These predictions prune a predefined, compact trajectory library, enabling the planner to proactively avoid dead ends while maintaining navigational smoothness. Notably, our approach transfers across real-world scenarios without manual annotation or fine-tuning on real-world data. The system achieves high-frequency replanning at 50 Hz onboard. Extensive simulation benchmarks demonstrate superior performance in success rate, flight time, and trajectory length, and real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness in complex scenarios.

</details>


### [258] [Throwing a Tight Spiral American Football by a Humanoid Robot](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16642)
*Zaid Mahboob,Bowen Weng*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Spin-stabilized, controlled tight spiral throw of an American football by a humanoid robot, achieving high spin efficiency and precise nose-angle alignment via coupled whole-body control and a two-phase upper-body strategy, validated on a 29-DoF robot with a 7-DoF gripper; demonstrates explicit spin injection at detachment and robust release handling at high speed.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Accurate spin control and release dynamics are critical for aerodynamically anisotropic objects (like American football). Prior robotic throwing work largely used open-gripper schemes and did not explicitly control spin injection during detachment, leaving spin/trajectory regulation underexplored especially during the sub-100 ms release when the ball is partially in contact. A coupled control framework is needed to realize precise, high-DoF motions and robust contact management.

Method: Develop a coupled whole-body control strategy where the lower body stabilizes the robot while the upper body operates in two phases: (i) a throw phase using trajectory optimization and tracking to accelerate the football to a target state, and (ii) a follow-through phase using model predictive control to actively control the wrist and remaining contact fingers. The system handles high DoF maneuvers within ~0.5 s and the sub-100 ms release when the ball is underactuated. Empirical validation on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid with a 7-DoF Dex3-1 gripper.

Result: Experimental results show the thrown football attains up to 93.6% spin efficiency and a 0.286 rad nose-angle error, at linear velocity up to 5.35 m/s and angular velocity 14.5 rad/s, with spin stabilization approaching an ideal tight spiral (100% spin efficiency, 0 rad nose-angle error).

Conclusion: The framework enables explicit spin injection control and effective handling of transient contact dynamics during release, achieving high spin stability and accurate trajectory for robotic football throwing. The approach demonstrates the feasibility of sophisticated, high-DoF, fast-release manipulation on humanoid platforms and suggests potential applicability to other spin-stabilized, aerodynamically sensitive objects.

Abstract: Accurate throwing of the American football requires precise regulation of release conditions, where coupled linear and angular momentum determine flight stability and targeting accuracy. While prior work on robotic object throwing has largely focused on generating dynamically feasible release velocities using open-gripper paradigms, explicit control of spin injection at detachment remains underexplored, particularly for aerodynamically anisotropic objects like the American football. In this paper, we present the spin-stabilized controlled tight spiral throw of an American football by a humanoid robot. Achieving this requires (i) accurately reaching the desired coupled momentum, which often involves high degrees-of-freedom (DoF) movements completed within approximately half a second, and (ii) managing the complex transient contact dynamics that arise during the sub-100-millisecond release phase, when the football is effectively underactuated as it moves partially across the fingers. To this end, we develop a coupled whole-body control strategy where the lower body is performing informed stabilization while the upper body is further divided into two phases with (i) a throw phase accelerating the football to a target state through trajectory optimization and tracking, and (ii) a follow-through phase utilizing model predictive control to actively control the wrist and remaining in-contact fingers. The proposed framework is empirically validated on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid equipped with a 7-DoF Dex3-1 three-fingered gripper. The thrown American football reaches up to 93.6% spin efficiency and a 0.286 radians linear-velocity-to-nose-alignment (nose-angle) error (where an ``ideal'' tight spiral corresponds to 100 % spin efficiency and 0 radians nose-angle error) at up to a 5.35 m/s linear velocity and an angular velocity of 14.5 rad/s.

</details>


### [259] [Orbit-Planner: Towards Latent World Models for On-Orbit Obstacle Avoidance of Satellite Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16651)
*Zhijian Li,Chao Ren,Peijin Wang,Xian Sun*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A two-stage latent world model, Orbit-Planner, enables on-orbit obstacle avoidance by learning action-conditioned spacecraft dynamics for latent future rollouts and a Physics Probe that decodes physical state changes from imagined trajectories; achieving long-horizon planning and high success in closed-loop Isaac Sim navigation (91.7%); code released.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Conventional planners rely on predefined maps and fixed environmental assumptions, limiting adaptability in dynamic, data-constrained on-orbit environments.

Method: A two-stage latent world model that (1) learns action-conditioned spacecraft dynamics to perform future-state rollouts in latent space, and (2) uses a Physics Probe to decode physical state changes from imagined latent trajectories.

Result: Demonstrates long-horizon latent rollouts and recovery of physical states from imagined trajectories; achieves 91.7% success in closed-loop obstacle-avoidance navigation in Isaac Sim.

Conclusion: Orbit-Planner shows effective latent-dynamics-based planning for robust, adaptable on-orbit obstacle avoidance and provides a practical code release for reproducibility.

Abstract: Satellite agents for on-orbit navigation tasks need to predict collision risks using limited onboard observations. However, conventional planners often rely on predefined maps and fixed environmental assumptions, limiting their adaptability in dynamic on-orbit scenarios. In this paper, we propose Orbit-Planner, a two-stage latent world model for on-orbit obstacle avoidance. Orbit-Planner learns action-conditioned spacecraft dynamics to perform future-state rollouts in latent space, and introduces a Physics Probe to decode physical state changes from imagined latent trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that Orbit-Planner can perform long-horizon latent rollouts and recover physical states from imagined trajectories. In closed-loop obstacle-avoidance navigation in Isaac Sim, it attains a success rate of 91.7%. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhijianLi2003/Orbit_Planner.

</details>


### [260] [H-PAC Hand: Control-Oriented Modeling and Tendon-Elasticity Compensation for an Underactuated Robotic Hand](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16712)
*Teng Yan,Jiongxu Chen,Teng Wang,Yue Yu,Qixiang Hua,Zihang Wang,Yongru Chen,Bingzhuo Zhong*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Proposes H-PAC: a modular 6-actuator, 15-DoF underactuated hand with a sparse actuator–joint model and a mechanics-based tendon-elasticity compensation, implemented in a hierarchical control setup; demonstrates substantial improvement in joint-angle accuracy without task-specific retuning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Tendon elongation under restoring-spring loads causes configuration-dependent joint deviations in underactuated, tendon-driven hands; a control-oriented model and compensation are needed to improve posture reproducibility in compact hands.

Method: Derives a sparse analytical actuator–joint model from tendon-routing geometry; develops a mechanics-based compensation for tendon-elasticity-induced joint errors; implements a hierarchical control architecture with a host computer for posture mapping and compensation and an ESP32 driving six position-controlled servos; reuses control parameters across tasks without retuning.

Result: Monotonic servo-sweep experiments show substantial compensation benefits: index DIP MAE reduced from 1.15° to 0.18°; all nine joints reach MAE < 0.23°, enabling postures and grasp configurations to be executed with the same control pipeline without external sensing in the loop.

Conclusion: A practical, generalizable approach to improving posture reproducibility in compact underactuated end-effectors by combining geometry-based actuation models with tendon-elasticity compensation and a consistent control pipeline.

Abstract: Underactuated tendon-driven hands offer compact actuation and passive compliance, but tendon elongation under restoring-spring loading introduces configuration-dependent joint deviations. This paper presents H-PAC, a modular 6-actuator, 15-DoF robotic hand with a control-oriented modeling and implementation framework. A sparse analytical actuator-joint model is derived from the tendon-routing geometry, and a mechanics-based compensation model is developed to account for tendon-elasticity-induced joint errors.
  The proposed method is implemented in a hierarchical architecture: a host computer performs workspace-constrained posture mapping and compensation, while an ESP32 generates synchronized commands for six position-controlled servos. The same control parameters and execution strategy are used across all tasks without task-specific retuning.
  Monotonic servo-sweep experiments show that the compensation substantially improves joint-angle prediction. The MAE of the index DIP joint decreases from 1.15 degrees to 0.18 degrees, and all nine evaluated joints achieve an MAE below 0.23 degrees. Representative postures and grasping configurations are further executed using the same control pipeline without external joint or force sensing in the control loop. The results demonstrate a practical approach to improving posture reproducibility in compact underactuated robotic end-effectors.

</details>


### [261] [MatchingPolicy: Correspondence-Aware Policy Enables Cross-Object In-Context Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16715)
*Qijin She,Hanyang Yu,Zeming Li,Ping Tan*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Proposes MatchingPolicy, a two-stage, correspondence-driven in-context imitation learning framework that decouples demonstration-to-scene matching from policy learning and uses a diffusion-based policy conditioned on dense correspondences; achieves strong few-shot generalization to unseen objects and categories on RLBench and real-world tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: In-context imitation learning often struggles to generalize to unseen objects and scenarios due to misalignment between matching demonstrations and action adaptation; robust out-of-distribution transfer remains challenging in robotic manipulation.

Method: Introduce MatchingPolicy with a separation between demonstration-to-scene matching and policy learning. A correspondence-aware diffusion policy conditions actions on dense semantic correspondences. A two-stage matching algorithm integrates vision foundation models to establish reliable correspondences, enabling robust matching across object instances and semantic categories.

Result: Empirical evaluations on RLBench and real-world manipulation tasks show superior few-shot performance and reliable generalization to unseen object instances and semantic categories.

Conclusion: Explicit decoupling of correspondence identification from action adaptation and a dense correspondence-conditioned policy improves out-of-distribution robustness and few-shot generalization in robotic manipulation.

Abstract: In-context imitation learning enables few-shot policy generalization but struggles to maintain performance on unseen objects and novel scenarios. To address this, we introduce MatchingPolicy, a correspondence-driven framework that explicitly decouples demonstration-to-scene matching from policy learning. Central to our method is a correspondence-aware diffusion policy that conditions robotic actions directly on dense semantic correspondences. This architectural separation resolves the inherent conflict between correspondence identification and action adaptation, enabling robust out-of-distribution transfer. Our framework integrates vision foundation models with a novel two-stage matching algorithm to dynamically establish reliable correspondences. Extensive evaluations on RLBench and real-world manipulation tasks confirm that MatchingPolicy achieves superior few-shot performance, generalizing reliably across unseen object instances and semantic categories.

</details>


### [262] [Design Optimization for Large High-Force Soft Robot Manipulators Under Gravitational Loads](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16728)
*Isara Cholaseuk,Penelope Llibre,Alexa Kyriacou,Audrey Wang,Akua K. Dickson,Ran Jing,Juan C. Pacheco Garcia,Andrew P. Sabelhaus*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Closed-form optimization of soft robot limb geometry to maximize blocking force under gravity with an anti-buckling constraint; validated experimentally on three pneumatically actuated geometries; enables a-priori design screening for large soft manipulators.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the lack of a systematic framework for selecting a design paradigm for large soft robots and to quantify the ability to generate high interaction forces safely under self-weight.

Method: Formulates an optimization problem to maximize end-effector blocking force subject to an anti-bucking constraint and gravitational loading, with an explicit (closed-form) solution under certain simplifying assumptions; experimental validation with three geometries of a large pneumatic manipulator.

Result: The method correctly predicts which designs satisfy the constraints and identifies the design that yields the largest end-effector forces; the closed-form solution supports rapid a-priori design screening.

Conclusion: A closed-form design tool enables a priori assessment of whether a given class of large soft manipulators is suitable for high-force physical interaction, potentially accelerating the design process for large-scale soft robotic actuators.

Abstract: Designing large soft robots capable of generating high forces for physical human-robot interaction remains a significant challenge in soft robotics. Prior work in large soft robots has focused on proof-of-concept prototypes, and no systematic framework exists for determining the suitability of a design paradigm for a desired task. This manuscript introduces a method for optimizing the geometry of a soft robot limb, maximizing its blocking force subject to an anti-bucking constraint under its own gravitational loading. We demonstrate that an explicit solution exists to the proposed optimization problem under certain assumptions. Experiments with three geometries of a large, soft, pneumatically-actuated manipulator demonstrate that the method correctly predicts which designs meet constraints and which produces the largest end-effector forces. This method, with its closed-form solution, can allow designers to determine a-priori if an intended class of soft manipulators is an appropriate choice for physical interaction at large size scales.

</details>


### [263] [Semantic- and Density-Aware Planning for Accessibility-Preserving Multi-Object Placement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16741)
*Benno Wingender,Nils Dengler,Nicolas Busch,Sicong Pan,Maren Bennewitz*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Introduces Semantic-Dense Placement Planning (SDPP) and an Accessibility Map for online shelf placement to jointly optimize semantic organization, space density, and accessibility; demonstrates improvements in simulation and a real-world demonstration.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Long-term manipulation planning requires considering how current decisions affect future interactions, especially in partially occupied shelves with unknown future arrivals; existing methods fail to jointly optimize semantics, density, and accessibility.

Method: SDPP ranks candidate poses using a semantic-density score that blends inter-object semantic similarity with spatial proximity; an Accessibility Map filters out unreachable placements and penalizes reductions in accessible workspace; integrated with motion planning; evaluated in simulation and a real-world qualitative demo.

Result: SDPP yields higher semantic placement quality and shelf density versus baselines; AM reduces time to identify feasible placements; qualitative real-world experiment demonstrates applicability.

Conclusion: SDPP advances online shelf-placement by trading off semantic grouping, dense utilization, and accessibility; AM efficiently prunes candidates, making the pipeline practical for domestic shelf-storage tasks.

Abstract: Long-term manipulation planning requires robots to reason not only about immediate task success but also about how current decisions affect future interactions with the environment. In this context, household service robots may need to organize groceries in partially occupied shelves while using limited storage space efficiently and preserving access for subsequent placements. In this paper, we consider an online multi-object shelf-placement setting in which future objects arrivals are unknown. Existing approaches do not jointly address semantic organization, dense space utilization, and manipulator accessibility during sequential shelf filling. To address this gap, we propose Semantic-Dense Placement Planning (SDPP), an accessibility-preserving approach that ranks candidate poses using a semantic-density score combining inter-object semantic similarity with spatial proximity. An Accessibility Map (AM) further filters candidates unlikely to be reachable before motion planning and penalizes placements that reduce the remaining accessible workspace. Simulation experiments show that SDPP significantly improves semantic placement quality over state-of-the-art baselines and achieves the highest average shelf density, while the AM substantially reduces the time required to identify feasible placement poses. A qualitative real-world experiment demonstrates the applicability of our pipeline in a domestic shelf-storage scenario.

</details>


### [264] [Neurosymbolic Embodied Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16794)
*Mohammad Albinhassan,Yuming Feng,Alessandra Russo,Pranava Madhyastha*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A neurosymbolic agent combines goal-directed visual exploration with constrained symbolic planning to ensure executable, long-horizon household task plans, achieving high success in simulation environments with 4B-27B models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the gap where language/vision models produce plausible but non-executable plans due to grounding and dynamics by enforcing executable plans through a guided, two-phase architecture.

Method: Phase 1: extract goal predicates and instance bindings from egocentric observations and grounded interactions via a vision-language model and exploration to form a symbolic initial state. Phase 2: use a PDDL transition model to constrain decoding to applicable actions; apply Monte Carlo tree search with a domain-independent heuristic to evaluate executable continuations. Plans are executable by construction under the transition model and transferred to the environment only with correct visual grounding.

Result: Open 4B-27B models achieve >90% task success on VirtualHome and ALFWorld; the smallest agent outperforms a 27B direct visual policy. Combining constraints and search solves >95% of ALFWorld tasks, whereas either alone solves under a third. The method uses fewer generated tokens and fewer model-visible images than alternatives; residual failures stem from state acquisition rather than planning, with no specialized training required.

Conclusion: Neurosymbolic integration of grounded vision with constrained symbolic planning and search yields robust executability guarantees and strong performance across embodied tasks, highlighting the complementary nature of constraints and search in long-horizon planning.

Abstract: Language and vision-language models generate plausible embodied plans but do not guarantee executability, as their outputs can violate environment dynamics or act on incorrectly grounded entities. We present a neurosymbolic agent that factors long-horizon household tasks into task-directed visual exploration and constrained symbolic planning. In the first phase, a vision-language model and exploration harness acquire goal-relevant predicates and instance bindings from egocentric observations and grounded interactions, producing a symbolic initial state. In the second, a PDDL transition model restricts decoding to tokens that extend applicable actions. Monte Carlo tree search then evaluates executable continuations using a domain-independent planning heuristic. The resulting plans are executable by construction under the transition model, with transfer to the environment conditioned on correct visual grounding. On VirtualHome and ALFWorld, open 4B-27B models exceed 90% success in both environments, and our smallest agent substantially outperforms a 27B direct visual policy in each. Constraints and search prove complementary rather than interchangeable: in ALFWorld either alone solves under a third of tasks, whereas their combination solves over 95%. The method also uses several times fewer generated tokens than extended thinking and far fewer model-visible images than direct interaction, and residual failures localize to state acquisition rather than plan generation without any specialized training.

</details>


### [265] [When State Becomes an Attack Surface: State-Semantic Injection in LLM-Driven Embodied Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16806)
*Jiawei Liu,Jiacheng Guo,Tian Zhang,Yiwei Xu,Juan Wang,Jinlin Fan,Bowen Xiao,Chi Guo,Keyan Guo,Hongxin Hu*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: LLMs are increasingly integrated with perception and robotic control to form embodied agents capable of task understanding, planning, and execution across modalities, demonstrated by multiple complementary approaches and models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Enable autonomous robots to ground language in scene understanding, object attributes, spatial relations, and execution feedback, leveraging LLMs to plan and reason and coordinating with robotics skill execution.

Method: Overview of multiple strategies: (1) SayCan—merges LLM task reasoning with robotic skills; (2) Code as Policies and ProgPrompt—generate robot task plans via policy code and programmatic prompting; (3) VoxPoser—combines language models with vision-language models to create 3D value maps for manipulation; (4) Vision-language-action models PaLM-E, RT-2, GR00T N1—tighter language–vision–action integration; and (5) grounding involves scene states, object attributes, spatial relations, and execution feedback, with plans handed to skill libraries, motion planners, or controllers.

Result: The abstract is not empirical; it asserts that these LLM-driven embodied agents can understand instructions, ground them in states/attributes/relations/feedback, plan actions, and hand off to executors; the practical performance is not quantified in the abstract.

Conclusion: LLM-driven embodied robotics is a promising paradigm that unifies language, perception, and action; the surveyed approaches collectively advance grounding and planning to enable autonomous robotic behavior, with future work focusing on robust grounding, real-time feedback, and seamless tool integration.

Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated capabilities in in-context learning, task decomposition, step-by-step reasoning, and code generation, driving their gradual evolution from text generation models into the core of agents capable of perceiving environments, invoking tools, and executing tasks. Traditional LLM Agents typically obtain information through webpages, documents, databases, or external tools and generate corresponding invocation sequences according to user goals; when this technology is further integrated with robotic systems, large language models begin to undertake functions such as task understanding, high-level planning, and behavioral decision-making. SayCan combines the task reasoning capability of language models with the affordances of robotic skills, while Code as Policies and ProgPrompt generate robot task plans through policy code and programmatic prompting, respectively, and VoxPoser uses language models and vision-language models to construct three-dimensional value maps to guide robotic manipulation \cite{6,7,8,9}. Vision-language-action models such as PaLM-E, RT-2, and GR00T N1 further strengthen the connection among language, visual perception, and robotic actions \cite{10,11,12}. In such LLM-driven embodied agents, the model not only needs to understand user instructions, but also needs to combine scene states, object attributes, spatial relations, and execution feedback to complete task grounding, and then hand the generated action plan to skill libraries, motion planners, or controllers for execution.

</details>


### [266] [Adaptive Repulsive Pheromone Clustering for Foraging Robot Swarms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16822)
*Carlos Pena-Caballero,Constantine Tarawneh,Qi Lu*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: ARPC uses repulsive pheromone waypoints clustered near the nest to demote revisiting explored regions, guiding robots toward unvisited areas, yielding up to 60% improvement in resource collection over CPFA/GPFA, validated in ARGoS simulations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: CPFA's tendency to revisit explored regions and neglect other areas reduces search efficiency as resources become scarce; a mechanism to diversify exploration and reduce redundancy is needed.

Method: Robots deposit repulsive pheromone waypoints at explored locations. Waypoints are clustered around the nest to estimate low-value regions; robots redirected toward likely unvisited areas. Integrates exploitation of known resources with systematic avoidance of redundancy. Evaluated via ARGoS simulations across arena sizes, resource densities, and spatial distributions (clustered, random, power-law).

Result: ARPC consistently outperforms CPFA and GPFA; early discovery gains around 10%; late-stage collection gains up to 60% under various conditions.

Conclusion: ARPC provides a scalable, robust strategy for large-scale heterogeneous swarm foraging, improving search diversity and resource discovery efficiency in sparse resource environments.

Abstract: The Central Place Foraging Algorithm (CPFA) combines site fidelity, pheromone-guided navigation, and uninformed random search to enable decentralized resource collection in robot swarms. However, CPFA often revisits previously explored regions while leaving other areas insufficiently searched, reducing efficiency as resources become scarce. In this paper, we propose Adaptive Repulsive Pheromone Clustering (ARPC), a bio-inspired method in which robots deposit repulsive pheromone waypoints to mark previously explored locations. These waypoints are clustered around the nest to estimate low-value search regions, allowing robots to be redirected toward likely unvisited areas. By integrating the exploitation of known resources with systematic avoidance of redundant exploration, ARPC improves search diversity and resource discovery efficiency. Extensive simulations in ARGoS across varying arena sizes, resource densities, and clustered, random, and power-law spatial distributions demonstrate that ARPC consistently outperforms CPFA and the Grid-Based CPFA (GPFA). In particular, ARPC yields significant gains during both early discovery (10\%) and late-stage (up to 60\%) collection, where conventional methods typically degrade. These results indicate that ARPC provides a scalable and robust strategy for large-scale heterogeneous swarm foraging environments.

</details>


### [267] [HAF: Adapting Generalist VLAs to Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-manipulation via Hierarchical Action Flow and Spectral Latent RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16837)
*Langzhe Gu,Chengkai Hou,Meng Li,Xinhua Wang,Jiaming Liu,Xinyuan Lv,Bowei Zhang,Shuanghao Bai,Guangrun Li,Jingyang He,Gaole Dai,Ziluo Ding,Zhiyuan Xu,Kuan Cheng,Jian Tang,Zhengping Che,Shanghang Zhang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A two-stage framework (HAF) transfers generalist VLA models to humanoid loco-manipulation via (i) HAF-VLA: a hierarchical, staged action generator with cross-stage KV caches to preserve kinematic dependencies; and (ii) HAF-Steer: a latent offline-to-online RL pipeline using flow-matching invertibility and DCT-based dimensionality reduction to restrict optimization to a compact noise subspace, keeping the VLA backbone frozen. Demonstrated on seven real-world tasks, it outperforms single-stage VLA baselines in whole-body coordination and task performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation:  tackle the high dimensionality and interdependence of humanoid whole-body motion, the suboptimality of offline imitation learning, and the safety/compute costs of online RL when adapting large VLA backbones to humanoid loco-manipulation.

Method: HAF-VLA: hierarchical action-flow generator built on a pretrained flow-matching VLA; splits full-body action denoising into three sequential stages with stage embeddings and cross-stage KV caches to retain dependencies. HAF-Steer: latent offline-to-online RL that leverages flow-matching invertibility and DCT-based dimensionality reduction to constrain RL optimization to a compact noise subspace and train a regularized SAC policy; the VLA backbone remains frozen.

Result: Outperforms vanilla single-stage VLA baselines on seven real-world humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, with improved whole-body coordination and task performance.

Conclusion: Shows the viability of transferring generalist VLA foundation models to humanoid loco-manipulation via a two-part framework that enables safe, data-efficient real-world refinement without updating the large backbone.

Abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet generalist vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models are not readily applicable to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation. The high dimensionality and interdependence of humanoid motions make it challenging for conventional single-stage VLA architectures to coordinate locomotion, waist posture, and dual-arm manipulation effectively. Moreover, policies trained through offline behavior cloning can remain suboptimal during real-world deployment. Although online reinforcement learning can refine policies through real-world interaction, directly tuning large VLA backbones demands excessive computation and may introduce safety risks during real-robot exploration. To address these bottlenecks, we introduce HAF (Humanoid Adaptation Framework), a two-part framework consisting of HAF-VLA and HAF-Steer that transfers off-the-shelf generalist VLA foundation models to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation. HAF-VLA is a hierarchical action-flow generator built on a pretrained flow-matching VLA. It splits full-body action denoising into three sequential stages with stage embeddings and cross-stage KV caches that retain kinematic dependencies, avoiding incoherent whole-body actions from one-shot generation. On top of the frozen HAF-VLA, HAF-Steer is a latent offline-to-online RL pipeline that leverages flow-matching invertibility and DCT-based dimensionality reduction to restrict RL optimization to a compact noise subspace and train a regularized SAC policy. This avoids updating the large VLA backbone and enables efficient real-world policy refinement. Evaluated on seven real-world humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, HAF surpasses vanilla single-stage VLA baselines and improves whole-body coordination and task performance. Project website: https://grange007.github.io/HAF .

</details>


### [268] [Security of Foundation-Model-Powered Embodied Agents: Attack Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16843)
*Jiawei Liu,Jiacheng Guo,Tian Zhang,Yiwei Xu,Juan Wang,Jinlin Fan,Bowen Xiao*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A trust-boundary-centric taxonomy of foundation-model-powered embodied-agent security, organizing attacks across five layers and twelve surfaces, based on 58 attack records and 61 defense records (through Aug 15, 2026).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To locate adversarial entry points within the embodied control loop and provide a boundary-focused framework separating attack surface from attack mechanism, enabling clearer analysis of propagation, defenses, and evaluation.

Method: Five-layer, twelve-surface taxonomy of the system (model supply chain, user instructions, context/memory, physical environments, perception, world state, internal reasoning, planning, action interfaces, middleware, multi-agent communication, execution control); compilation of 58 attack records and 61 defense records up to 2026-08-15; cross-layer propagation analysis, defense placement assessment, and evaluation-practice review.

Result: Attack research is concentrated on multimodal perception and action interfaces; defenses are concentrated on action-level and runtime protection. Underexplored areas include context/long-term memory, middleware/networking, world-state integrity, and multi-agent trust. Quantitative synthesis and qualitative insights highlight open challenges and gaps.

Conclusion: Open challenges identified: state provenance, compositional defenses, long-horizon attack propagation, physical realizability, Byzantine multi-robot behavior, and unified closed-loop evaluation; the framework enables targeted defense placement and future research directions.

Abstract: Foundation models are increasingly used for perception, reasoning, planning, and action generation in embodied agents, creating security risks that can propagate from digital inputs to physical behavior. Existing surveys often organize threats by mechanisms such as jailbreaks, prompt injection, backdoors, poisoning, or adversarial examples, but these categories do not consistently identify where an adversary first enters the embodied control loop. We present a trust-boundary-centric survey of foundation-model-powered embodied-agent security. Using a first-compromised-trust-boundary principle, we separate attack surface from attack mechanism and organize the system into five layers and twelve attack surfaces spanning the model supply chain, user instructions, context and memory, physical semantic environments, multimodal perception, world state, internal reasoning, task planning, action interfaces, middleware, multi-agent communication, and execution control. Based on 58 attack records and 61 defense records collected through August 15, 2026, we analyze representative attacks, cross-layer propagation, defense placement, and evaluation practices. Our quantitative analysis shows that attack research is concentrated on multimodal perception and action interfaces, while defenses are especially concentrated on action-level and runtime protection. Context and long-term memory, middleware and networking, world-state integrity, and multi-agent trust remain comparatively underexplored. We conclude with open challenges in state provenance, compositional defenses, long-horizon attack propagation, physical realizability, Byzantine multi-robot behavior, and unified closed-loop evaluation.

</details>


### [269] [FlexWorm: Primitive-augmented Hybrid Contact-motion Planning for Suction-based Multi-segment Deformable Robots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16853)
*Zili Tang,Tiecheng Guo,Qinyue Zhang,Meng Guo*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A planning framework for serial multi-segment suction-based soft robots enabling 3D navigation with discrete adhesion switching and continuous deformation, via block-wise IK hybrid search (IKHS) and primitive-augmented hybrid search (PaHS).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the reliance on manually designed gaits and environment-specific motion scripts by enabling autonomous, constraint-aware planning for deformable soft robots on complex surfaces.

Method: Block-wise IK hybrid search (IKHS) performs best-first search over feasible adhesion transitions and solves inverse kinematics only on induced free blocks. Primitive-augmented hybrid search (PaHS) augments IKHS with a learned observation--primitive embedding to retrieve short, validated motion segments for fast local proposals, with fallback to standard IKHS branching.

Result: In simulation, the framework outperforms controlled baselines in planning success, transition quality, and efficiency across diverse terrains. PaHS matches IKHS in success rate while substantially reducing planning time. Hardware experiments with a pneumatic multi-segment soft robot demonstrate executability and online recovery under actuation and adhesion uncertainty.

Conclusion: The framework enables robust, 3D navigation for deformable multi-segment soft robots with adhesion switching by combining a feasible-block IK-based search with learned, retrieval-based local proposals, improving planning efficiency without compromising feasibility and enabling online recovery in hardware.

Abstract: Multi-segment suction-based soft robots are promising for inspection and maintenance in confined or fragile environments, but existing approaches still depend heavily on manually designed gaits and environment-specific motion scripts. This work presents a planning framework for serial multi-segment soft robots with deformable body segments and boundary suction pads. The formulation targets full 3D navigation on complex surfaces and explicitly handles discrete adhesion switching and continuous body deformation under geometric, collision, and quasi-static feasibility constraints, while remaining agnostic to the specific actuation realization used to produce segment deformation. Its core, block-wise IK hybrid search (IKHS), performs best-first search over feasible adhesion transitions while solving inverse kinematics only on induced free blocks. On top of IKHS, primitive-augmented hybrid search (PaHS) uses a learned observation--primitive embedding to retrieve short validated motion segments for fast local proposal, with fallback to standard IKHS branching when retrieval fails. In simulation, the framework consistently outperforms controlled baselines in planning success, transition quality, and efficiency across diverse terrains. PaHS matches IKHS in success rate while substantially reducing planning time. Repeated hardware experiments on a pneumatic multi-segment soft robot further demonstrate executability and online recovery under actuation and adhesion uncertainty.

</details>


### [270] [$τ_0$-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16885)
*Xiaowei Cai,Yunuo Cai,Bingao Chen,Jingxiao Chen,Zhi Chen,Siyuan Feng,Tengyu Hou,Jingshun Huang,Han Jiang,Runkun Ju,Dong Li,Mingxiang Li,Shaowei Li,Xinchen Li,Yifan Li,Yi Liu,Zhongyuan Liu,Jianlan Luo,Junwen Miao,Ruiqi Ni,Buqing Nie,Mingjie Pan,Xinlin Ren,Jianheng Song,Jiaxu Wang,Peiqi Wang,Sen Wang,Xiaoyan Wang,Dafeng Wei,Dongming Wu,Pengwei Xie,Pu Yang,Hangjian Ye,Xiangyu Yue,Jinyu Zhang,Qinglin Zhang,Xueyong Zhao,Pengfei Zhou,Yue Zhou*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: τ0-VLA introduces a compute-scalable hierarchical VLA model for long-horizon robot manipulation, enabling test-time computation to refine subtask planning via world-model guidance, improving prediction and success.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current hierarchical VLA models rely on single forward passes, limiting decision quality under difficult or consequential choices and across long sequences.

Method: High-level policy with execution memory generates subtasks; when needed, it searches over alternatives (test-time computation) guided by a world model; a low-level policy executes the chosen subtask across several robot embodiments; trained on 40,115 hours of heterogeneous real-world data with multimodal co-training.

Result: Allocating additional test-time computation substantially improves next-subtask prediction accuracy in both in-domain and distribution-shifted settings, translating into higher closed-loop success on long-horizon tasks.

Conclusion: The proposed compute-scalable inference framework enhances planning quality and robustness for long-horizon robot manipulation and generalizes across embodiments, suggesting a practical path for scalable, reliable robot intelligence.

Abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to both execute individual skills reliably and sequence them coherently over extended tasks. Most hierarchical vision-language-action (VLA) models make each such decision with a single forward pass, leaving no mechanism to allocate additional computation to difficult or consequential choices. We introduce $τ_0$-VLA, a hierarchical robot foundation model that formulates high-level subtask generation as a compute-scalable inference problem through world-model-guided test-time computation. At each inference step, the high-level policy uses execution memory to generate a subtask and, when needed, searches over alternatives before committing to its output. A low-level policy then executes the generated subtask across multiple robot embodiments. The policy is trained on 40,115 hours of heterogeneous real-world data with multimodal co-training. Across in-domain and distribution-shifted settings, allocating additional test-time computation substantially improves next-subtask prediction accuracy, and these gains translate into higher closed-loop success on long-horizon robot manipulation tasks.

</details>


### [271] [Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16889)
*Bingxin Xu,Yuzhang Shang,Emilio Ferrara*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: BATON tackles long-horizon robot manipulation by subtask-level exploration and transition-aware memory, addressing multiplicative exploration costs and missing entry/exit conditions in VLA-based planning. It reuses stored subtask solutions to compose long-horizon plans, adds verifications and handoff/lookahead transitions, and updates no parameters.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: In long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation, errors cascade and subtasks constrain future steps. Vision-language-action policies struggle due to multiplicative test-time exploration and lack of explicit transition representations between subtasks.

Method: BATON makes each subtask the unit of exploration, stores its solution in memory, and composes long-horizon trajectories from these solutions. It introduces a transition-aware memory with a verifier agent that gates VLA calls, and uses handoff and lookahead transitions to restore entry states and select transferable strategies.
